setting.name: Solo play
setting.hint: For playing alone. The Realm keeps its Myths, Landmarks and Barriers from the Referee as it does from players, until the Company finds them. A Myth is named once one of its Omens is met, and its hex shown once the Company stands in it.

welcome.label: Playing alone
welcome.hint: The Realm's Myths, Landmarks and Barriers stay hidden from you too, and turn up as the Company travels. You can change this later in the Toolkit's Settings.

solo.unknownMythHint: Nothing is known of it until one of its Omens is met.
solo.mythFound: The Company has found the hex of Myth {number}.
solo.newMythText: A new Myth stirs in the Realm. It will be known by its first Omen.
solo.panelLocked: While playing alone, what stands in a hex isn't changed here, so nothing still to be found is given away.

sheet.title: Mythic Bastionland
sheet.armourOn: Its Armour counts. Click when it doesn't apply.
sheet.armourOff: Its Armour doesn't count. Click when it applies.
sheet.armourIdle: Worn, but its Armour doesn't count right now. Click to take it off.
sheet.holdsOn: It holds now, so this piece’s Armour {counts}. Click when it doesn’t.
sheet.holdsOff: It doesn’t hold now, so this piece’s Armour {counts}. Click when it does.
sheet.empty: Nothing yet. Drag an item here or add one.
sheet.newKnightHint: Roll up a Knight from the book on this sheet. The new scores, Property, Ability and Passion replace the ones here. Scars stay.
sheet.chooseKnightedHint: Roll or choose which Knight this Squire became. Their Virtues, GD and everything they carry stay, and the Knight’s Property, Ability and Passion are added.

heraldry.title: Heraldry of {name}
heraldry.lineHint: Drag from one end to the other. Hold Shift to keep it level, upright or diagonal.
heraldry.eyedropperHint: Click the shield to take a colour from it. Alt-click does the same with any tool.
heraldry.divisionsHint: Pick a division, then click a part of the shield to paint it, and the parts matching it, in the colour in hand.
heraldry.downloadHint: Save this design to your computer, to upload again later.
heraldry.downloadFailed: The design could not be turned into a file to download.

placing.title: Picture
placing.hint: Drag it to move it. Scroll over it, or use the slider, to change its size. It keeps a layer of its own, to move or change whenever you pick it again.
placing.doneHint: Back to the paints. Pick its layer to change it again.

layers.title: Layers
layers.addHint: Add an empty layer to paint on, straight above the layer picked.
layers.empty: Each thing painted, placed or rolled goes on a layer of its own, to bring forward or send back.

heraldry.layersTooLarge: The layers were too large to keep on the Knight, so the heraldry was saved as one picture. Ask the GM to let you upload files to keep them.

charges.openHint: Place a lion, a tower, a star or another charge on the shield, in the colour in hand, on a layer of its own.
charges.title: Charges
charges.hint: Click a charge to place it on the shield in the colour in hand.
charges.credit: Drawn after public-domain heraldry books by Mathghamhain Ua Ruadháin for the Book of Traceable Heraldic Art. © 2016–2023 Matthew Simon Ryan Cavalletto, CC BY-SA 4.0.

heraldry.randomizeHint: Roll random arms over the whole shield: a field, plain or divided, and perhaps a charge, in tinctures that read well against each other. The field and charge go on layers of their own; anything else on the shield stays. Change any part of them afterwards, or roll it again. Undo brings the last design back.

arms.title: Arms
arms.hint: Change any part, or roll it again with its die. Drag the charge to move it, and scroll over it to resize it.
arms.doneHint: Back to the paints, to paint by hand on a layer of its own. Edit arms, or picking the arms' layers, brings these controls back.
arms.editHint: Change these arms' field, tinctures or charge.
arms.rollField: Roll another field, divided another way and in new tinctures
arms.rollTinctures: Roll new tinctures for the field and charge
arms.rollCharge: Roll another charge, keeping its colours and place
arms.counterchange: Counterchange: the charge takes the field’s colours swapped about, part by part

heraldry.unreadable: That picture couldn’t be loaded onto the shield.
heraldry.tooLarge: This heraldry is too detailed to keep on the Knight. Simplify it, or ask the GM to let you upload files.

glory.label: Glory
glory.title: Glory
glory.hint: Won when a Myth you played a part in is resolved, by a staked duel or joust, a tournament, a battle remembered in history, or when a new Age begins.
glory.nobody: Nobody was ticked, so no Glory is awarded.

myth.label: Myth Resolved
myth.intro: Tick every Knight who played a part in the Myth. Each gains 1 Glory.
myth.hint: Once the table agrees the Myth has ended, however it ended.

tournament.label: Tournament Won
tournament.intro: Tick the winning Knight. They gain 1 Glory.
tournament.hint: Only a tournament with a real crowd and real pageantry earns Glory.

battle.label: Battle Won
battle.intro: Tick every Knight on the victorious side. Each gains 1 Glory.
battle.hint: Only a battle big enough for the chronicles earns Glory.

successor.label: Successor
successor.hint: The Knight or Squire named to follow this Knight. Succession names them, and Legacy passes on half of this Knight’s Glory.
successor.empty: No successor named. Drop a Knight here, or choose one.
successor.name: Name a Successor
successor.title: Name a Successor
successor.intro: Whom does {name} name as their successor?
successor.none: There’s no other Knight or Squire in this world for {name} to name.
successor.noLegacy: Legacy: no successor named, so no Glory passes on.
successor.legacy: Legacy: {name} gains {amount} Glory, half of theirs.

seer.label: Seer
seer.unnamed: Write the Seer who knighted them above, beside “Knighted by”. A Seer from the book fills in their picture and what the book says.
seer.infoEmpty: Filled in from the book once the Seer beside “Knighted by” is one of the book’s and Import PDF has been run.

npcPack.label: NPCs
npcPack.seeded: NPCs: {seers} Seers and {cast} of the Casts are now in the {pack} compendium, for you to drag into the world as they’re met.

squire.label: Squire
squire.empty: In a Company of 2 Knights or fewer, each Knight may have a Squire. Take one, or drag a Squire here from the Actors tab.
squire.servesNobody: A Squire who serves no Knight. Drag this Squire onto a Knight’s sheet.
squire.hint: An apprentice rather than a Knight: no Glory and no Feats until they’re Knighted, when each Virtue rises by d6.
squire.name: Squire to {knight}
squire.title: A Squire
squire.largeCompany: Squires are for a Company of 2 Knights or fewer, and this one has {count}. Take a Squire anyway?
squire.largeCompanyPlayer: Squires are for a Company of 2 Knights or fewer, and this one has {count}. Ask the Referee.
squire.largeCompanyHint: The Company has {count} Knights, and Squires are for a Company of 2 or fewer.
squire.largeCompanyHintGM: The Company has {count} Knights, and Squires are for a Company of 2 or fewer. As Referee you may grant one anyway.
squire.companyGrew: The Company now has {count} Knights, and Squires are for a Company of 2 or fewer. Squires in this world: {squires}. Whether they stay is the Referee’s call.
squire.cantCreate: Taking a Squire creates them and their pony, so it needs a user who is allowed to create actors.
squire.knightConfirm: {name} becomes a Knight, gaining d6 in each Virtue. From then on they can gain Glory and perform Feats. Then choose which Knight they became: they keep everything they have.

fatigued.label: Fatigued
fatigued.hint: No Feats again until they’ve rested.

exhausted.label: Exhausted
exhausted.hint: At VIG 0 from Virtue Loss: no Attack in a turn you’ve already moved.

exposed.label: Exposed
exposed.hint: Treated as having 0 GD until they remedy it, as a rest once the danger has passed does. CLA 0 also leaves you Exposed.

impaired.label: Impaired
impaired.hint: At SPI 0 your Attacks roll a single d4 only, with no bonus dice or Feats.

mortalWound.label: Mortal Wound
mortalWound.hint: Down and dying: no Attacks or Feats. An hour without help kills them, but a few moments’ care patches them up.
mortalWound.down: {name} is Mortally Wounded, down and dying, so they can’t Attack or use Feats until they’re patched up.

slain.label: Slain
slain.hint: Taken to VIG 0 by Damage: dead. VIG 0 from Virtue Loss only leaves them Exhausted. Raising VIG above 0 lifts it.

wounded.label: Wounded
wounded.hint: Took Damage past their GD. Lasts until their VIG is whole again. Armour worn only when Wounded counts.

mounted.label: Mounted
mounted.hint: On horseback: a lance counts as Hefty, and armour worn when mounted counts.

recovery.label: Recovery
recovery.vig: Sustenance, or a day of hospitality
recovery.afterCombat: The fight is over. Restore Guard for {names}, and leave them no longer Fatigued or Exposed?
recovery.restedAfterCombat: The danger has passed: {names} restore Guard, and are no longer Fatigued or Exposed.
recovery.rested: A moment’s calm: GD restored to {value}, and no longer Fatigued or Exposed.
recovery.restIntro: {name} takes a moment’s calm, once the danger has passed (Recovery, p9).
recovery.restWhat: GD returns to full, from {value} to {max}. Fatigue is removed, and they are no longer Exposed. A card in chat says so.

unchosen.hint: Nobody has claimed this Knight yet. Roll or pick one from the book, or fill in the sheet yourself.
unchosen.hintGM: Nobody has claimed this Knight yet. Choose one now, or give them to a player to choose.
unchosen.hintViewer: Nobody has claimed this Knight yet.
unchosen.byHand: Fill in the sheet by hand

ledger.buttonHint: Every change made to this Knight, who made it and when
ledger.title: {name}: Ledger
ledger.deleteMany: Delete these {count} lines from the Ledger? This can’t be undone.

knighthood.title: Knighthood
knighthood.unread: Import your rulebook PDF to read pp6–7 here in the book’s own words.

property.label: Property
property.hint: What the Knight brings with them. Every Knight also carries rope, torches, dry rations, camping gear and a dagger (d6).
property.keepsPlace: {name} keeps its place: weapons come first, biggest die leading, then shields, then armour from the head outward, then everything else.

apply.title: Which Possession?
apply.which: More than one possession could take what {column} gives. Which is it about?
apply.blankDetail: The result stays on the table, and no possession changes.
apply.applied: {item} is now as the table says.
apply.none: Nothing of {name}’s could take what {column} gives, so it stays on the table.

knightTable.intro: Roll a d6 for each column, or click a heading to roll just that one. Click an entry to take it instead.
knightTable.introViewer: What this Knight rolled on the table from their page.
knightTable.missing: This Knight has no table from the book yet. Import PDF, or choose them from the book, to fill it in.

1-01.1: The symbol wakes when someone is {entry}.

1-02.1: Your companion’s past has left them {entry}.

1-03.1: You are called to battle by {entry}.
1-03.2: Your fancy helm is crowned with {a entry}.

1-04.1: You drink {entry} to fuel your rage.
1-04.2: Your hatred of {entry} stokes your rage.

1-08.1: The Armour found you at the {entry}.

1-10.1: Under the moon your body turns {entry}.

1-11.2: Your bird is specially trained in {entry}.

2-03.2: The taste of home comes from {entry}.

2-04.1: You can {entry} without giving yourself away.

3-02.2: Whatever you drink from it tastes of {entry}.

3-10.2: The sword was given to you by {entry}.

4-03.1: You have a blind spot for {entry}.

4-06.2: Your explosive is set off by {entry}.

4-08.1: The Cleavingblade came out of {a entry}.
4-08.2: It came to you at a time of {entry}.

4-11.1: Your flute’s song is loved by {entry}.
4-11.2: Your flute’s song is hated by {entry}.

5-02.1: You keep the bones in {a entry}.

5-06.1: The snake speaks in {a entry} voice.

5-08.2: It is patched together with {a entry}.
