6-05.1: To form the cocoon you must be {entry}.

6-10.2: Your scroll names an ancestor of {entry}.

6-11.1: How do you know it came from the sea? {entry}.

steed.label: Steed
steed.empty: Take a steed, or drag an NPC from the Actors tab here to ride it. Its trample joins a mounted charge.
steed.namePlaceholder: Leave empty to name it later
steed.blankIntro: Take a steed with no stats yet, to fill in yourself.
steed.blankDetail: A steed of your own, with a trample to fill in on its sheet.
steed.pickIntro: Take one of the book’s steeds (p12), or one with no stats yet to fill in yourself.

gallop.title: Gallop
gallop.intro: Tick everybody galloping. Each rides 2 Hexes this Phase, and their steed loses d6 VIG (p18).
gallop.exhaustedNow: {steed} is Exhausted, and can’t Gallop again until its VIG is restored.
gallop.hint: Only a steed that isn’t Exhausted can Gallop.

steed.cantCreate: Taking a steed creates it as an NPC, so it needs a user who is allowed to create actors. Ask the GM, or drag a steed here from the Actors tab.
steed.fromDirectory: Drag the steed from the Actors tab rather than a compendium, so it can be targeted in combat.
steed.cannotCreate: You can’t make new actors, so {names} stayed on the sheet as Property. Ask the GM to make them NPCs, then drag the steed onto the Steed box.

remedy.intro: Tick everybody present. Each has their {virtue} restored, and the Remedy is used up.
remedy.hint: A Remedy takes a whole Phase to use, and its Virtue comes back before anything the Phase brings, Omens included.
remedy.limit: {name} already carries a Remedy, and nobody, person or pack beast, can carry two. Give it to somebody else to carry.
remedy.limitSteed: {name} already carries a Remedy, and nobody, person or pack beast, can carry two. {steed} could carry it.

ability.label: Ability
ability.usesHint: Leave blank for an Ability with no limit. Once its time comes round, its uses are all back.
ability.lastingDieHint: In a Combat, its row has a button adding this die to every Attack until the fight is over. It spends a use, if it has a limit.
ability.addLasting: Add {die} for the rest of the fight
ability.grantsHint: Offered in the Attack dialog. One with uses is offered unticked, and spends a use when ticked. One with no limit comes ticked.
ability.readUsesHint: Fill in the uses from words such as “twice per day” in the description.
ability.noUsesRead: Nothing in {name}’s description says how many uses it has and when they come back.
ability.bonusDieHint: Added to an Attack it’s used in, as a charge’s +d12. Offered in the Attack dialog.
ability.needsHint: The Attack dialog refuses it in any other kind of Attack.

powers.rerollPool: Rolls a joint Attack’s pool again
powers.rerollPoolHint: A joint Attack card offers its Knight a button to roll every die again, once, before anything is spent on them.
powers.deathWardHint: When somebody nearby would be Mortally Wounded or Slain, applying the Damage asks whether this Knight takes the Mortal Wound instead.
powers.coinFlip: Flips a coin for a life
powers.coinFlipHint: Its row has a coin: with one Token targeted, heads it dies, tails this Knight does.
powers.sigil: Etches a rune for a number
powers.sigilHint: Its row has a star: at sunset, pick a number. A die showing it on an Attack card can be turned to another face, as many times as the number, until the next sunset.

passion.label: Passion
passion.indulged: {name} indulges their Passion, {passion}. SPI restored to {value}.

feats.label: Feats
feats.knightHint: All three Feats are known to every Knight.

smite.name: Smite
smite.summary: A melee Attack gains d12, or Blast.

focus.name: Focus
focus.summary: A Gambit that costs no die.

deny.name: Deny
deny.summary: Strike out one die of an Attack on you or an ally beside you.

feats.alreadyFatigued: {name} is Fatigued: no Feats again until they’ve rested.

gambits.label: Gambits
gambits.repel: Repel: push the foe back from you
gambits.stop: Stop: the foe can’t move on their next turn
gambits.impair: Impair: a weapon of theirs is Impaired on their next turn
gambits.trap: Trap: their shield is held until your next turn
gambits.hint: Each Gambit spends one Attack die showing 4 or more. Except for Bolster and Move, the foe may make a VIG Save to shrug it off.
gambits.strong: Strong Gambit: a melee die of 8+ also grants No Save or a Greater effect.

card.tagline: Gambit: discard an Attack die of 4 or higher
card.save: The target may make a VIG Save to ignore it.
card.noSave: The target gets no Save against it.
card.target: It can only affect somebody this Attack was aimed at.

marks.impair: {name}'s Impair Gambit Impairs a weapon of yours for your next turn.
marks.stop: {name}'s Stop Gambit stops you moving on your next turn.
marks.trap: {name}'s Trap Gambit holds a shield of yours until their next turn, so leave it out of this Attack.
marks.impairWeapon: {name}'s Impair Gambit Impairs your {weapon} for your next turn: an Attack with it rolls a single d4, but your other weapons still fight.
marks.clear: Clear this once it has run its course.

details.move: A Move that works even after moving, or when movement is otherwise barred.
details.dismount: A rider knocked from the saddle takes d6 Damage, added to the Attack’s dice in combat.

morale.title: Morale
morale.hint: Roll when Wounded, or when a group loses half its number. An organised group rolls once, on its leader’s SPI.
morale.askIntro: {name} makes a SPI Save to hold firm rather than rout or surrender (Wavering Morale, p10). Roll when Wounded, or when a group loses half its number.
morale.askWhat: A d20 is rolled against their SPI of {value}: {value} or less holds firm. On a failure, the card offers to mark them Fled or Surrendered, which takes them out of the Combat’s turn order.
morale.notOwner: Only a GM or {name}’s owner can roll their Morale.

fled.label: Fled
fled.hintOne: They rout. Marks them Fled on their sheet, and takes them out of the Combat’s turn order.
fled.hint: The group routs together. Marks each of them Fled, and takes them out of the Combat’s turn order.

surrendered.label: Surrendered
surrendered.hintOne: They surrender. Marks them Surrendered on their sheet, and takes them out of the Combat’s turn order.
surrendered.hint: The group surrenders together. Marks each of them Surrendered, and takes them out of the Combat’s turn order.

broke.clear: Clear it: they’re back in the fight
broke.notOwner: Only a GM or their owner can say how their Morale broke.
broke.already: That’s already marked on their sheet.

triggers.wounded: {name} is Wounded: a SPI Save, or they rout or surrender.
triggers.halved: {name} has lost half its number: a SPI Save, or it routs or surrenders.

group.title: Wavering Morale
group.intro: {down} of {count} on this side are down. The rest make a SPI Save, or rout or surrender.
group.noneStanding: Nobody you control in this group is still standing.

organised.label: Organised
organised.hint: An organised group rolls once, on its leader’s SPI.

disorganised.label: Disorganised
disorganised.hint: A disorganised group rolls for each individual, on their own SPI.

duel.title: Duel
duel.buttonHint: Target the one Token you’ve agreed to duel, then press this.
duel.needTarget: Target the one Token you’ve agreed to duel, then press Duel.
duel.intro: {name} and {opponent} agree to fight. It goes as any fight does, except both Attacks, Gambits and all, are rolled and settled at once, and either may use Feats first.

duel.label: Duel
duel.hint: Two combatants who mutually agree to fight.

duel.stakeHint: Fought in public, a duel or joust can have Glory staked on it, if both agree: the winner gains 1, the loser loses 1.
duel.stakeKnightsOnly: Only two Knights can stake Glory, and a Squire isn’t a Knight yet.
duel.bloodlessHint: Training, or a duel that isn’t to the death. Scars only come from real, deadly combat, so it leaves none.
duel.sparringHint: A practice bout, whose Damage doesn’t last (p188). Nobody is left dying or Scarred, and each duelist’s GD and VIG are put back as they were when the duel ends.
duel.sparringNote: Sparring: nobody is left dying or Scarred, and each duelist’s GD and VIG are put back when the duel ends, the fight is over, or time passes.

shaken.title: Shaken Off
shaken.nothing: Neither duelist has anything to shake off.
shaken.combatEnded: The fight is over, and so is the bout.
shaken.timePassed: Time has passed, and the bout with it.

duel.stakeNote: Glory is staked: the victor gains 1, and the loser loses 1.
duel.bloodlessNote: Bloodless: a blow that would cause a Scar leaves none.
duel.howTo: Each duelist presses Attack on their sheet, then uses Feats and declares Gambits on their card. A GM, or whoever owns both, then resolves the two Attacks together.
duel.endedNoVictor: The duel ends without a victor.
duel.attackInSparring: Part of the {kind} with {name}, a sparring bout
duel.attackHint: Targets the other duelist, and holds the Damage back until both Attacks are in.
duel.heldForDuel: Part of a duel: the Damage is applied from the duel card, together with the other Attack.
duel.notReady: Both duelists need to roll their Attack first.
duel.gone: One of the duelists no longer exists.
duel.attackGone: One of the duel’s Attack cards has been deleted.
duel.cantResolve: Only a GM, or somebody who owns both duelists, can resolve their Attacks.
duel.cantEnd: Only a GM, or somebody who owns both duelists, can end the duel.
duel.noScar: {name} would take a Scar, but a bloodless duel leaves none.
duel.needsGM: A GM needs to be logged in to change somebody else’s duel card.
duel.changeRefused: The duel card changed before that could be recorded.

surprise.title: Roll Surprise
surprise.intro: Tick everybody who wasn’t readied for combat. Each makes a CLA Save or misses the first turn.
surprise.hint: The players usually go first, agreeing a plan and acting in whatever order they like.
surprise.skipped: {name} was caught unready and misses the first turn.
surprise.noCombatants: This encounter has nobody in it yet.
surprise.nobody: Nobody was caught unready, so there’s nothing to roll.

reaction.title: Reaction
reaction.buttonHint: A SPI Save for how they take it, when the Referee is uncertain which way they’d go.
reaction.favourable: Nothing unfavourable in how they take it.
reaction.hint: How someone takes things usually follows from the moment (p8). Roll only when it could go either way.
reaction.askIntro: {name} makes a SPI Save for how they take it (Reaction, p8). Roll only when the Referee is uncertain which way they’d go.
reaction.askWhat: A d20 is rolled against their SPI of {value}: {value} or less, and nothing is unfavourable in how they take it; any higher, and they take it badly. A card in chat shows the result.

skyWeather.tick: Roll the day’s sky and weather
skyWeather.tickHint: The Nature Spark Tables’ Sky and Weather set the scene as the Company wakes and breaks camp (p197).
skyWeather.title: The Day’s Sky and Weather
skyWeather.cardHint: Describe it as the Company breaks camp. Be kind by default, but let hard weather bite when the dice call for it (p197).
skyWeather.missing: Run the Import PDF macro with your rulebook to bring in the Nature Spark Tables’ Sky and Weather.

fog.solid: Solid Fog: the Knights can’t see into the neighbouring hexes, and without a way to keep their course they’re travelling blind until the day is out (p197).
fog.maybe: Fog: if it’s thick enough to hide the neighbouring hexes, bring it down and the Company may be travelling blind (p197).
fog.down: Let the Fog Hide the Way
fog.fell: Fog hides the way until the day is out.
fog.pastDay: That weather was rolled for another day, so it can’t bring fog down or lift it today.
fog.vantage: Fog hides the land around, so from here the Company makes out nothing past this Hex (p197).

travel.title: Fog Hides the Way
travel.text: Fog hides the neighbouring hexes. Without a way to keep their course the Company is travelling blind, and rolls each time it moves to a new Hex this Phase (p197).

travels.title: Places
travels.asPlayers: As the players see it: nothing they haven’t found. Only the chosen hex’s Rolled Here, at the foot of it, is yours alone.
travels.none: The Company hasn’t been anywhere on this Realm yet.
travels.notVisited: The Company knows nothing of {hex} yet.
travels.notKnown: The Company knows nothing of this hex yet.

sections.ofNoteHint: Where the Company found something, was told something or wrote a note.
sections.heardOfHint: Told of, written about or seen from afar, but not reached yet.

chart.title: The Company’s chart of the Realm
chart.route: Show the way the Company went
chart.zoomHint: Hold Ctrl and turn the wheel over the chart, or double-click it, to zoom in; then drag it about with either button.

journey.none: The Company hasn’t set out on this Realm yet.
journey.arrivedFirst: Came to {place} for the first time
journey.met: {name} was turned back by the {direction} Barrier of {place}

detail.empty: Choose a hex in the list, on the chart or in the journey to see what the Company knows of it.

gm.heading: Rolled Here
gm.hint: For GMs only: what the players haven’t found here, and what the Lay of the Land keeps for the hex.
gm.fillHint: Roll the land, its weather and one feature on the Nature Spark Tables, and keep them in this hex.

met.when: {direction} Barrier: {name} was turned back by it here, in {when}.
met.plain: {direction} Barrier: {name} was turned back by it here.

party.heading: The Company’s Note
party.placeholder: What the Company makes of this place, for everyone at the table
party.needsGM: A GM has to be here to keep the Company’s note. Your words are still in the box.
party.offline: The note can be written while a GM is here.
party.refused: The Company’s note couldn’t be kept. Your words are still in the box.

controls.marks: Mark the Hexes Visited (right-click to choose the mark)

marks.title: Visited Marks
marks.hint: How the hexes the Company has been to are marked on a Realm, in this browser only: a pencilled ring, a tick, a cross or the hex’s edge drawn over, each in a colour of your choosing.
marks.shown: Mark the hexes the Company has been to
marks.shownHint: In this browser only: everyone else keeps their own. The footprints beside the sidebar do the same.

pencil.label: Pencilled Ring
pencil.detail: A faint dashed line just inside the hex, leaving its middle clear.

tick.label: Tick
tick.detail: A tick across the middle of the hex.

cross.label: Cross
cross.detail: A cross through the middle of the hex.

edge.label: Hex Edge
edge.detail: The hex’s own border drawn over in a strong line.

seenFromAfar.title: Seen from Afar
seenFromAfar.intro: From the vantage point the Company can make out that something stands in these hexes, but not what it is.
seenFromAfar.rule: Each one ticked gets an unnamed mark on the players’ map until the Company gets there (p197). Add a few words of what they see, if you like.
seenFromAfar.placeholder: What they see, such as a structure, smoke rising
seenFromAfar.marked: {count} marked on the players’ map as seen from afar.
seenFromAfar.reached: The Company has reached what it saw from afar, and it is shown on the players’ map.

phaseEnd.title: The {phase} Ends
phaseEnd.nowhere: No Realm shows where the Company stands, so no Wilderness Roll is made.
phaseEnd.spent: How did the Company spend the {phase}?
phaseEnd.alreadyOpen: The Phase is already ending. Finish that window first.

travel.label: Travelling or exploring
travel.hint: On the move, or searching the Hex. Through the Night this costs d6 SPI each and leaves no time for proper sleep.

camp.label: Camping outdoors
camp.hint: Sleeping outdoors. The Wilderness Roll ignores Landmarks, and a hostile Omen prevents proper sleep.

indoors.label: Indoors, as guests
indoors.hint: Travelling Knights are owed a roof by custom. A night indoors needs no Wilderness Roll.

wilderness.omen: Show the next Omen of the Myth in this hex, with no roll
wilderness.none: A Holding isn’t Wilderness, so there’s no Wilderness Roll.
wilderness.barrier: Make the Wilderness Roll, which an attempt on a Barrier still causes
wilderness.indoors: Spent indoors, there’s no roll whatever is ticked.

rules.travel: Travelling or exploring through the Night costs d6 SPI each, and leaves no time for proper sleep.
rules.winter: Winter: d6 VIG from each who camped out or travelled by night.
rules.dire: Dire weather held through the Night, so nobody outdoors got proper sleep.
rules.each: Tick who else went without proper sleep, such as for a hostile Omen (d6 CLA), and who was deprived of essential needs (d6 VIG).

dying.rule: Nobody Mortally Wounded outlives an hour without care, and a Phase is longer than that. Untick anybody who was tended; Patch Up on their sheet clears the wound.
dying.title: Died Untended
dying.line: Left Mortally Wounded and untended, they die.
dying.hint: An hour without care kills the Mortally Wounded; a few moments of it patches them up (p8).

time.title: Time

banner.weeksHint: Continue on to the next seasonal event ({event}).
banner.yearHint: A new Age, starting in Spring.

phaseHints.morning: From sunrise until noon. Whoever slept badly loses d6 CLA, and whoever went without food, water or fire loses d6 VIG.
phaseHints.night: From sunset until sunrise. Moving about by night costs each d6 SPI, and with no guide and no light the Company travels blind.

time.seasonIntro: {season} gives way to {next}. Each Knight ticked has their Virtues restored and chooses a pursuit, and any Mutilation Scar settles.
time.ageIntro: Age {age} begins in Spring. Each Knight ticked has their Virtues restored, gains 1 Glory and chooses a pursuit. Old Knights lose d12 VIG, and any Mutilation Scar settles.

agePick.title: The Age
agePick.turn: Turning the Age begins Age {next} in Spring. Each Knight taking part has their Virtues restored, gains 1 Glory and chooses a pursuit, and Old Knights lose d12 VIG.
agePick.setHint: Setting the Age only puts the number right. Nothing that comes between Ages happens.
agePick.change: Turn the Age, or set it by hand

time.noCompany: There are no Knights in this world yet, and no Tokens are selected.

service.question: What small improvement to the Realm did {name}’s Service make?
service.dwelling: A Dwelling added to the map

made.dwelling: Service: a new Dwelling, marked on the map.
made.other: Service: the Realm made a little better.

service.markIt: The Dwelling brush is in hand: click the hex where the Service made it.
service.openRealm: Open the Realm and mark the new Dwelling with the Landmark brush in Paint the Realm.

courtesy.question: What did {name}’s Courtesy earn?
courtesy.joined: Courtesy: a place at the Court of {court}, as a Courtier.
courtesy.noCourt: Courtesy: a place at Court, though no Domain is kept yet to write it in.

distant.hint: A journey to a distant Realm usually ends in the Season after this one.
distant.title: Journey to a Distant Realm
distant.where: Which Realm does the Company journey to? Choosing one of this world’s Realm Scenes makes it the active Scene once they arrive.
distant.intro: The Company journeys to {realm}, arriving in {season}. Each Knight ticked has their Virtues restored as the Season turns, and any Mutilation Scar settles. Nobody chooses a pursuit, since they are on the road.

time.oldAge: Old age: loses {amount} VIG, max VIG {from} → {to}.
time.doomLifts: The Season of their Doom has passed, and a Mortal Wound no longer Slays them.

due.title: Due this Season
due.crisis: The Crisis Roll for {domains} (p20), from the GM Toolkit’s Time page or each Domain’s sheet.
due.drama: Drama in Court for {domains} (p21), from each Domain’s sheet.
due.myths: A new Myth in place of each one resolved: {myths} (p27), from the GM Toolkit’s Time page.
due.emptySeats: {domain} has nobody as {seats} (p20). A Domain runs smoothly only with its seats filled.
due.designs: Grand Designs done (p21): {works}. Strike them off each Domain’s sheet.

time.unresolvedHint: Roll an Unresolved Situation for anything important left hanging.
time.winterReminder: It’s Winter: camping out or travelling by night costs d6 VIG, and dire weather may keep the Company where it is.

events.title: The Season’s Events
events.hint: Each Season begins with a Feast, sees a mass at its middle, and ends with the Realm’s collection (p17). The book doesn’t number a Season’s days, so these come in the order they come rather than on a date.
events.markHint: Mark this event as having come to pass, and tell the table.
events.passedHint: This event of the Season has already come to pass.
events.endsHint: The Realm’s collection ends the Season, so it comes to pass as the Season turns.
events.weeksHint: On to the next seasonal event that matters (p17). Reaching the Realm’s collection turns the Season instead.
events.weeksPassed: Weeks pass on the road, and a new Morning dawns.
events.nextIs: Weeks passing carries the Company on to {event}.
events.nextIsEnd: Only {event} is left, which ends the Season, so weeks passing turns the Season.
events.collected: Collected by {domains}, whose Stewards may press their Vassals for more to pay for a war or a great work.
events.nothingLeft: Every event of {season} has come to pass, so only the Season’s end is left. Turn the Season.
events.notThisSeason: {event} isn’t an event of this Season, or has already come to pass.

feastOfTheSun.label: The Feast of the Sun
feastOfTheSun.prompt: A feast is a fine place for a Knight to be seen, and for a Vassal to ask a favour of one.

sceptremass.label: Sceptremass
sceptremass.prompt: Every ruler in one hall: a good moment for drama in Court (p21), or for a Knight to press a claim their rank is unworthy of.

tax.label: The Tax
tax.prompt: The usual collection keeps a Domain going comfortably. A Steward who wants more, for a war or a great work, has to roll for it (p21).

feastOfTheStars.label: The Feast of the Stars
feastOfTheStars.prompt: A tournament with a real crowd and real pageantry earns its winner 1 Glory (p6).

eldermass.label: Eldermass
eldermass.prompt: Every Seer knows each Myth’s rules, secrets and whereabouts, and their guidance restores CLA. None of it comes for free.

tithe.label: The Tithe
tithe.prompt: The usual collection keeps a Domain going comfortably. A Steward who wants more, for a war or a great work, has to roll for it (p21).

feastOfTheMoon.label: The Feast of the Moon
feastOfTheMoon.prompt: The dead are named tonight: a Knight’s Scars, their Doom, and the successor they have yet to establish.

kindlemass.label: Kindlemass
kindlemass.prompt: Every door open: a whole day as somebody’s welcome guest restores VIG, and a night under a roof needs no Wilderness Roll.

levy.label: The Levy
levy.prompt: The usual collection keeps a Domain going comfortably. A Steward who wants more, for a war or a great work, has to roll for it (p21).

nightTravel.title: Travelling by Night
nightTravel.text: The Company is on the move by night. With no guide and no light they’re travelling blind, rolling for every Hex they try to enter this Night. What the Night costs is taken as it ends.

hardship.none: Nobody was ticked, so nobody loses anything.
hardship.notDamage: Virtue Loss isn’t Damage, so it can’t Mortally Wound or Slay.

night.label: Night travel
night.hint: Moving about by night costs each d6 SPI.

sleep.label: No proper sleep
sleep.hint: Each morning, all who didn’t get proper sleep the day before lose d6 CLA.

winter.label: Winter cold
winter.hint: In Winter, a night camped out or on the road costs each d6 VIG.

supplies.label: Deprived
supplies.hint: A morning that finds them without food, water or fire costs each of the Company d6 VIG.

aging.title: Growing Older
aging.intro: {name} becomes {age}. Roll each Virtue on d12+d6 for it?
aging.newAge: A new Age begins. Tick each character who grows a stage older. Each Virtue is rolled again on d12+d6: someone turning Mature keeps the higher result, someone turning Old the lower (p17).

domain.title: {name} Domain
domain.seatHint: Where the whole Realm is ruled from, with a Holding’s troubles writ large.

ruler.label: The ruler’s arms
ruler.detail: {name}’s arms, changing with whoever rules here.
ruler.none: No Knight rules here yet, so the shield stays blank until one does.

picture.label: A picture
picture.detail: An image of your choosing, shown square instead of a shield.

domain.successorHint: Whom the ruler names to follow them, or whom the Realm’s Seers or Knights-Elector choose instead. Expect some resistance either way. Pass On hands the Domain to them.

holding.label: Holding
holding.hint: The Holding on the Realm map this Domain rules. When its ruler’s Knight comes home with the Company after Weeks or a Season away, the Crisis Roll is offered.
holding.awayHint: Weeks or a Season have passed with the ruler away, so their return brings the Crisis Roll (p20). Weeks Pass and turning the Season tick this for a ruler away from the Holding; a Crisis Roll clears it.

homecoming.title: Home from a Long Absence
homecoming.text: {ruler} is back at {name} after a long absence.
homecoming.rule: Make the Crisis Roll as each Season begins, and on coming home after a long time away (p20).

newRuler.name: Or by name
newRuler.hint: Choose one of the world’s Knights, or write in anybody else. A Knight chosen here rules the Domain from their sheet.

passOn.buttonHint: Succession: hand the Domain to the ruler’s successor.
passOn.title: Succession
passOn.hint: In some Realms it’s not the ruler who chooses, but gathered Seers or Knights-Elector.
passOn.resistance: Whoever takes the seat meets some resistance, and does well to show their authority quickly.

conquest.buttonHint: Conquest: somebody seats themselves in this Holding and rules it.
conquest.title: Conquest
conquest.introSeat: Who seizes {name}, and with it the Realm, by force?
conquest.hint: Often, whoever is bold enough to take a Holding’s seat simply becomes its ruler.
conquest.turmoil: Taken by force and not contested, it is in turmoil for a time before it settles under its new ruler. The turmoil lasts until the Season turns.
conquest.inTurmoil: In turmoil: seized by force this Season, it hasn’t yet adapted to its new ruler.
conquest.settled: The turmoil of its conquest passes, and it adapts to the rule of {ruler}.

council.label: Council
council.empty: Nobody sits as {seats}. A Domain runs badly with its great seats empty, and trouble finds it.
council.hint: Set a Council member a task that takes anything from a Phase to a whole Season. It’s resolved like any other action, and failing it tends to bring a Crisis. You can grant and take away seats, but whoever loses one won’t forget it.
council.noRetainersHint: A seat goes to one of the Court’s Retainers. Take somebody on in the Court first, then grant them the seat here.

circle.label: The Circle
circle.empty: No Knights sit in the Circle
circle.title: The Circle
circle.intro: Which Knights does {name} seat in its Circle?
circle.noKnights: There are no other Knights in this world to seat.

tasks.scopeHint: How long the work takes. It can be settled sooner, but it isn’t due until then.
tasks.riskHint: What could go wrong? If nothing, there’s no roll; otherwise it’s settled by a Luck Roll or a Save (p16).
tasks.noSheet: {name} has no sheet to Save with, so it falls to a Luck Roll.
tasks.noOneSaves: Several Knights sit in the Circle and none makes the Save alone, so it falls to a Luck Roll.
tasks.setAsideConfirm: Is “{what}” taken back out of the {seat}’s hands? Nothing comes of it, and what was written goes with it.
tasks.everyCrisis: The Domain already faces every Crisis, so the Referee says what this failure brings instead.

success.label: The task is done.
success.hint: Things improve: a step forward, a threat weakened, or a trouble ended.

problem.label: The work is done, but something potentially bad comes of it.
problem.hint: Things get harder: a new trouble behind the finished work, or an old one grown.

crisis.label: It fails, and a Crisis comes of it.
crisis.hint: A failed Council task tends to bring a Crisis, which the Domain faces until it’s dealt with.

domain.crisisRollHint: Rolled as each Season begins, or on coming home after a long time away.
domain.rolledThisSeason: The Crisis Roll has been made this Season ({season}).
domain.notRolledThisSeason: The Crisis Roll hasn’t been made this Season yet ({season}).

crisis.dilemma: Dilemma: a choice between two Crises.

collections.crisis: The coffers are filled, but a Crisis comes with it.
collections.willing: The Vassals pay up, mostly without complaint.

drama.association: It concerns you through someone close.

domain.dilemmaIntro: {name} must take on one of these Crises.
domain.dilemmaOpen: No choice was made between {options}. Add the one chosen from the sheet.
domain.misruleHint: Vassals rise up, Knights ride away and pretenders press their claims.
domain.misruleDue: {count} unresolved Crises: if the Season ends like this, the Domain falls into misrule.
domain.fellIntoMisrule: The Season ended with {count} unresolved Crises, and the Domain falls into misrule.
domain.collectionsHint: A Steward presses the Vassals for more, to pay for a war or a great work.
domain.dramaHint: There’s drama at Court each Season. Roll to see how the ruler is drawn in.

designs.label: Grand Designs
designs.hint: Works the Domain has in hand (p21). Each is marked done once its time has come, and the Season’s card says so; strike it off with ×.

works.label: Work on what stands
works.hint: Repairs and additions to what already stands, usually done by the next Season.

building.label: A new building
building.hint: New buildings or infrastructure, completed in a Season: the next one if begun as a Season begins, the one after that otherwise.

grand.label: A grand project
grand.hint: Castles, roads and the like, a whole Age in the making: done as the next Age begins if begun as an Age begins, the one after that otherwise.

founding.title: Found a Domain
founding.name: Name
founding.nameHint: Left blank, it takes the Holding’s name.

court.label: The Court
court.hint: Everyone serving the ruler (p20). The Council’s great seats are granted to Retainers from here, and each Season’s drama falls to somebody here.
court.nobody: Nobody serves in the Court yet.
court.nameNeeded: Give them a name first. Nobody joins the Court without one.

retainer.notePlaceholder: What work do they aid with?

courtier.notePlaceholder: What honour or ambition do they hold?

petitioner.notePlaceholder: What do they ask for: help, advice, or judgement?

seer.notePlaceholder: Do they visit, or send an acolyte?

court.name: Name
court.rollName: Roll a name from the book
court.rollNameUnread: Import the rulebook first. Its names are read from the Knights’ pages.
court.servesHint: The Council member who took them on.
court.leverageHint: What hold they have over the ruler, such as kinship, secrets or swords (p21). Easy answers leave somebody aggrieved, so a ruler treads carefully.
court.leveragePlaceholder: What hold do they have over you?
court.removeConfirm: Does {name} leave the Court? What was written about this {role} goes with them.
court.removeConfirmSeated: Does {name} leave the Court? Their seat as {seat} stands empty, and what was written about this {role} goes with them.
court.noLeverage: Holds no leverage over the ruler, which is the ruler’s good fortune.
court.emptyHint: Nobody serves in the Court yet, so there is nobody for the drama to fall to.

domain.muster: Can muster {count} Warbands. The Marshal decides their training and armament.
domain.openHint: Open the Domain this Knight rules
domain.foundHint: This Knight rules no Domain yet. Found one, or drag a Domain here from the Actors tab.
domain.askNamed: {name} rules no Domain yet, but {domain} names them as its ruler. Make it theirs, or found a new Domain?
domain.cantCreate: Founding a Domain creates it, so it needs a user who is allowed to create actors. Ask the Referee, or drag an existing Domain onto this sheet.
domain.fromDirectory: Drag the Domain from the Actors tab rather than a compendium.

goods.foldersSeeded: Arms & Goods: added {items} items to the Items directory and {actors} beasts, hirelings, Warbands and structures to the Actors directory.

company.title: The Company
company.name: The Company
company.place: Place the Company on the map
company.pictureIntro: One Token stands for the whole Company, and this is the picture it carries on the Realm.
company.colourHint: The icon is drawn in this colour, with a halo behind it so it reads on any Realm.
company.colourFailed: The Company's colour could not be saved, so the icon is carried in ink.

lost.title: The Company has left the map
lost.text: Their Token was deleted at {hex}. One Token stands for the whole Company, and it has no Actor to reopen it from, so put them back here or stand them in a hex with Place the Company over the map.
lost.textAway: Their Token was deleted. Stand them in a hex again with Place the Company over the map.
lost.cannot: The Company is already on the Realm, or there is nowhere to put them back.

company.pictureHint: Choose one, or browse for a picture of your own. One you carry stays here to choose again.
company.tokenHint: One Token stands for the whole Company. It belongs to no Actor, so every player can move it.
company.forgetPicture: Take this picture out of the gallery. The file itself stays where it is.

wanderer.name: Wanderer
wanderer.hint: Young Knights-Errant, newly come to the Realm in search of Glory. You choose where they arrive.

courtier.name: Courtier
courtier.hint: Mature Knights-Gallant with a place in Court. The Company begins at the Seat of Power.
courtier.newsHint: Word of the nearest Myth’s first Omen reaches the Court as news (p6). It counts as met.

ruler.name: Ruler
ruler.hint: Mature Knights-Tenant. One rules a Holding, and something wicked has hold of the Seat of Power. You choose which Holding.
ruler.influenceNoPrompt: Something wicked has hold of the Seat of Power.
ruler.influenceHint: One Knight rules a Holding, with the rest of the Company in their Circle (p6). Where the Knights aren’t made yet, found the Domain later from the ruling Knight’s Domain button, ticking the others into the Circle.
ruler.domainQuestion: One Knight rules a Holding, with the rest of the Company in their Circle (p6). Which Knight rules?

company.begins: The Company begins at the Seat of Power, {hex}.

choose.wanderer: Wanderers arrive in the Realm: click the hex where they arrive.
choose.courtier: This Realm has no Seat of Power: click the hex where the Court sits.
choose.ruler: One Knight rules a Holding: click the hex of that Holding.
choose.anywhere: Click the hex the Company stands in.

placing.hint: One Token stands for the whole Company, and this Realm has none on it. Carry them over the map and click the hex they stand in.
placing.stop: Right click or press Escape to place them later.
placing.later: The Company waits off the map. Take them up again with Place the Company over the map.

bookFlip.title: Flip the Book
bookFlip.openHint: A random page of the book, for a prompt along its foot
bookFlip.hint: A random spread of the book and the prompts along its foot. Take whatever fits the blank you’re filling: a Hex, a stranger, an explanation (p19, p179). Click the prompts you’ll use, then Save to hex and click a hex on the map.
bookFlip.unread: Import PDF hasn’t read the prompts on this page.
bookFlip.chooseFirst: Click a prompt to choose it first.
bookFlip.noRealm: Open a Realm’s map to save to one of its hexes.
bookFlip.pick: Click the hex to save {what} to.

hexPick.stop: Right-click or press Esc to stop.

hexLore.title: The Lay of the Land
hexLore.hint: A Hex is broad and varied, with room enough for a person never to leave it. Roll the Spark Tables for what fills this one and write down what you made of it, so it’s the same Hex when the Company comes back (p19).
hexLore.notePlaceholder: The cliffs, the streams, the clearings and the caves.
hexLore.setMissing: Import PDF hasn’t read enough of the Nature Spark Tables to roll a wilderness hex.

wildHex.intro: A wilderness hex is rolled on the Nature page’s tables set out for it. Roll a d12 for each column, or click a table’s die or a heading to roll just that. Click an entry to choose it instead. Nothing is kept in the hex until you save the results.

landmark.reroll: Name it from a random page
landmark.rerollHint: Flip to a random page and take the prompt it prints for this Landmark’s type.

hexLore.nothingToTell: Write what’s in the hex before telling the players about it.
hexLore.told: Told the players about the hex at {hex}.
hexLore.toldOnce: Told the players once, in {when}. They keep what was said in their Places.
hexLore.toldMany: Told the players {count} times, last in {when}. They keep what was said in their Places.
hexLore.exploreHint: What the Company can learn of this Hex by asking, searching, and looking about (p19).

firstArrival.name: Roll a new hex’s land
firstArrival.hint: The first time the Company comes to rest in a Wilderness Hex with nothing written or rolled there, roll its land and one feature on the Nature Spark Tables, keep them in the Hex, and whisper them to the GM. Holdings are left alone.

prompt.name: Reaching a new hex
prompt.hint: What to do when the Company comes to rest in a Hex of a Realm you’re looking at. Saved per browser.

modes.open: Open the Lay of the Land

hexJournal.writtenOver: This page is written again whenever the hex changes, so edits made here will be lost. Change the hex in the Lay of the Land, or write in the GM Notes page.
hexJournal.openHint: Open this hex’s Journal entry: what the Company knows, and your own notes.
hexJournal.none: Nothing has been rolled or written for this hex yet, so it has no Journal entry.

setting.name: Journal entries for hexes
setting.hint: Each hex of a Realm that something is rolled or written for gets a Journal entry, kept up to date as you roll. Players can read its What the Company Knows page once they could open the hex in their Places. Its GM Notes page is yours and is never written over. What was rolled in a hex shows in Places and the Lay of the Land.

siteJournal.writtenOver: This page is written again whenever the Site changes, so edits made here will be lost. Change the Site on its map, or write in the Notes page.
siteJournal.routeOut: {kind} route from {from} to somewhere not yet explored
siteJournal.routeAway: {kind} route between places not yet explored
siteJournal.glimpsed: Places glimpsed but not yet explored: {count}
siteJournal.nothingFound: Nothing has been found here yet.
siteJournal.openHint: Open this Site’s Journal entry: the whole Site, what the Company has found, and your own notes. Players can’t see it until you share it.
siteJournal.none: Nothing has been drawn or written on this Site yet, so it has no Journal entry.

setting.name: Journal entries for Sites
setting.hint: Each Site with something drawn or written on it gets a Journal entry, kept up to date as you draw and reveal. It starts hidden from players. Share it when you like: players then see only its What the Company Found page, never The Site page or your Notes, which are never written over.

spark.title: Spark Tables
spark.hint: Roll a table for a d12 in each column, and combine the two into a prompt to improvise from.

keybinding.name: Open the Spark Tables
keybinding.hint: Open the Spark Tables, or close them when they’re already in front. Takes the hotbar’s 6 for the GM.

spark.keepNone: Open a hex’s Lay of the Land to keep rolls there
spark.keepHint: Rolls made here are kept in the hex the Lay of the Land is open on, or else the hex the Company stands in, beside the rest rolled there.
spark.noIndex: Run the Import PDF macro with your rulebook to bring in the Spark Tables.
spark.noText: Run Import PDF again with your rulebook to bring in the Spark Tables.
spark.pageMissing: The Spark Tables on this page couldn’t be read. Import PDF’s report says why.

people.rollHint: Roll every People Spark Table at once, for a ruler or a stranger to read from the lot (p200, p202).
people.title: A Person
people.missing: Run Import PDF with your rulebook to bring in the People Spark Tables.
people.nameHint: Enter keeps the name, Esc leaves it as it was

holding.rollHint: Roll the Holding on the Civilisation Spark Tables, two or three people there, and a Myth of the Realm each has heard of, and keep it all in this hex (p181).
holding.noMyths: This Realm has no Myths yet, so nobody here has heard of one.
holding.none: There’s no Holding in this hex to roll up.
holding.missing: Run Import PDF with your rulebook to bring in the Civilisation and People Spark Tables.

myths.noRealm: There’s no Realm Scene yet. Use New Realm in the Scenes tab to roll one.

weather.title: Weather
weather.hint: Choose the weather. FXMaster draws it on the Scene the players are on, and it follows them to the next. Each morning the day’s Sky and Weather roll sets it for you; pick another here if you see the day differently. Where dire weather rules the land, roll Dire Weather from the Referee Rolls.
weather.paused: The weather is off the map. Change it, or put it back
weather.resume: Put It Back on the Map

button.name: Show the Weather Button
button.hint: With FXMaster on, the GM Toolkit’s banner has a button for the weather. Untick this to hide it if you don’t use the weather. The weather last set stays and still follows the table; set it to Clear first for none. Saved per browser.

weatherOnMap.name: Weather on the Map
weatherOnMap.hint: With FXMaster on, the weather falls on the Scene the players are on. Untick this to take it off the map and keep it set, the same as Take It Off the Map in the weather picker.

weatherFxClouds.name: Clouds
weatherFxClouds.hint: The clouds drifting over the map, from a fair sky to a storm. Needs FXMaster.

weatherFxFog.name: Fog
weatherFxFog.hint: The fog over the map. Needs FXMaster.

weatherFxRain.name: Rain
weatherFxRain.hint: The rain, from a shower to a storm’s. Needs FXMaster.

weatherFxHail.name: Hail
weatherFxHail.hint: The hail in a storm. Needs FXMaster.

weatherFxSnowstorm.name: Blizzard Snow
weatherFxSnowstorm.hint: The driven snow of a blizzard. Needs FXMaster.

weatherFxStormTint.name: Storm Light
weatherFxStormTint.hint: The grey a storm casts over its clouds. Untick it and the clouds stay, untinted. Needs FXMaster.

card.title: Weather on the Map
card.text: The weather you pick in the GM Toolkit, and the one the day’s Sky and Weather roll brings each morning, can fall on the Scene your players are on: rain, fog, snow and storm clouds.
card.needs: It’s free. Install it from the Add-on Modules tab on Foundry’s setup screen, then turn it on for this world.
card.fine: Nothing else needs it, and the weather is still kept without it. Once it’s on, the Toolkit’s banner gets a weather button, where you can also take the weather off the map; single parts of it can be turned off under Settings.

gmToolkit.name: GM Toolkit
gmToolkit.rulebookSetup: Point this world at your rulebook PDF
gmToolkit.companyPictureHint: Change the picture the Company’s Token carries on the Realm, even before they’re on the map. Right-clicking the Token offers the same.
gmToolkit.noCompany: The Company isn’t on this Realm’s map
gmToolkit.relaunch: Launch the world again to get the GM Toolkit. The world was already open when the system added it.
gmToolkit.gmOnly: Only a GM can make the GM Toolkit.
gmToolkit.onlyOne: This world already has a GM Toolkit.
gmToolkit.keep: The GM Toolkit holds your notes, so the world’s last one can’t be deleted.

myths.hint: The Realm’s Myths, each with the Omen playing out and the one to come. Omens are met in order (p18). The Lay of the Land and the Wilderness Roll count the same Omens. For your eyes only.
myths.noText: Run Import PDF to quote each Myth’s Omens here.
myths.clickOmen: Click the Omen the Company has met, or it again to take it back
myths.markOmen: The Company has met Omen {number}: mark it, and cross out the ones before it
myths.unmarkOmen: Take this Omen back, leaving the one before it playing out
myths.notePlaceholder: Who has been met, what the Company knows, where it’s heading.
myths.resolvedHint: Once the table agrees a Myth is over, another takes its place next Season (p27).
myths.newMythTooltip: Roll d6 and d12 on the Myths table (p27) for the Myth that replaces this one, in the same hex and under the same number.
myths.chooseTooltip: Which six Myths the Realm holds: roll one again, roll them all again, or choose them from the book’s table (p27).
myths.newMythRolled: A new Myth in {hex}, replacing one resolved
myths.newMythHint: Its Omens start again from the first. Undo on the Realm takes the roll back, with your notes on the old Myth.
myths.showTable: Open the table beside the Omens
myths.tableReading: Reading this Myth’s table from your rulebook…
myths.tableMissing: Give the world your rulebook (press B), or run Import PDF, to bring in this Myth’s table.

cast.title: The Cast
cast.makeTooltip: Add them to the Actors directory as one of the Cast, with the stat block the book prints for them, in a folder named after this Myth.
cast.remove: Take them out of this Cast
cast.empty: Nobody here yet. Drag an actor onto this card to count them among the Cast.
cast.dropHint: Drag an actor onto this card to count them among the Cast.
cast.noText: Run Import PDF to read the printed Cast here. Until then, drag an actor onto this card to count them among it.
cast.fromDirectory: Import them into the world first: an actor in a compendium can’t be counted among a Cast.

visits.forgetConfirm: Every visit the Company made to {hex} is forgotten. What you wrote about the hex, and the Spark Tables rolled there, stay.
visits.foldHint: Strike out one visit, telling or note with its ×, or forget it all at once below. The Spark Tables rolled here go by their own × further down.
visits.forgetAllConfirm: Every visit the Company made to {hex}, the Spark Tables rolled there and what you wrote about it are all forgotten.
visits.forgetAllConfirmShared: Every visit the Company made to {hex}, the Spark Tables rolled there and what you wrote about it are all forgotten. So are what the players were told of it and their own note on it, which goes from their Places too.
visits.noTold: The players haven’t been told about this hex.
visits.noParty: The players haven’t written about this hex.

places.hint: Every place in the Realm and every hex the Company has come into, each once, with what you wrote about it and the Spark Tables rolled there (p19). A hex counts as visited once the Company’s Token walks into it, or when you count a visit by hand. These are the same notes as in the Lay of the Land. For your eyes only.
places.visitedNone: The Company hasn’t come into any hex of this Realm yet. Move its Token, or count a visit on a place below.
places.unvisitedHint: The Holdings and Landmarks, found or not, and any other hex you’ve written about or rolled for.
places.unvisitedNone: The Company has been to every place in the Realm.
places.othersHint: Hexes the Company has come into, or with something written or rolled, that hold no Holding or Landmark, such as a Myth’s hex.
places.othersNone: The Company hasn’t come into any other hex, and nothing is written about one yet.
places.trackedHint: The hexes you chose to keep an eye on, in the order you added them.
places.trackedNone: No places tracked yet. Add one below, or use Track This Place on any card.

track.title: Track a Hex
track.askHint: This Realm isn’t the scene on the map, so give the hex by its column and row.

places.sitesHint: Places explored in more detail than a Hex (p15).

time.crisisRollsHint: Every Domain makes its Crisis Roll as a Season begins (p20). These haven’t made it this Season yet.

gmToolkit.clockHint: Change the Season or Phase here to set the calendar by hand, and click the Age to turn it or set it by hand. Only the Time window’s buttons carry out what happens between Seasons (p17).

seasons.title: Past Seasons
seasons.hint: Each Season you wrote about, the Myths resolved in it, and what passed as it ended, as its card told the table. Turning the Season, the Age, or journeying to a distant Realm fills it in. Setting the calendar by hand doesn’t. For your eyes only.
seasons.noMyth: No Myth was completed this Season.
seasons.notesPlaceholder: What the Company did, who they met, what was left hanging.
seasons.notRecorded: The calendar was moved off this Season by hand, so nothing was recorded as it ended.

notes.hint: Your own notes. When a session ends, ask what the players mean to do next time, and write it here (p16).

cityQuest.title: The City Quest
cityQuest.hint: Once the Company is worthy of the City Quest, a Wilderness Roll of 1 brings an Omen of the City in place of a random Myth’s. Roll d12, add the Omens of the City already met, and take the next one down for one already seen.
cityQuest.noText: Run Import PDF again to quote the Omens of the City here.
cityQuest.seen: Omens of the City encountered: {count}. The City Quest ends after Omen {end} or higher.
cityQuest.roll: Roll an Omen of the City
cityQuest.ends: Omen 18 or higher: after this Omen, the City Quest ends.
cityQuest.resetConfirm: Every Omen of the City encountered is forgotten, as for a new Company.
cityQuest.wildernessHint: This Company is worthy of the City Quest, so an Omen of the City comes in place of a random Myth’s. It follows below.

draw.label: Draw
draw.hint: Mark points, draw routes and place entrances.
draw.help: Click a point to mark it, or the gap between two marked neighbours to draw a route.

reveal.label: Reveal
reveal.help: Players see the points they’ve found, with the open and closed routes from them. Click a point, a hidden route or an entrance to show or hide it.

sites.rollRestHint: Follow the book’s steps for whatever isn’t done yet, keeping everything already drawn.
sites.clearConfirm: Erase every point, route and entrance, and what’s written about them? The rules and the notes on the Site stay.
sites.showPlayersHint: Show this Site to players. They see only what they’ve found.

feature.label: Feature
feature.hint: A circle. Something to learn here, or a sense of the place.
feature.placeholder: What’s here to learn, or to feel?

danger.label: Danger
danger.hint: A triangle. Something to get past with care.
danger.placeholder: What has to be got past with care?

treasure.label: Treasure
treasure.hint: A diamond. Something worth the finding.

open.label: Open
open.hint: A solid line. An easy way from one point to the next.

closed.label: Closed
closed.hint: A crossed line. The way is blocked, and getting past takes some ingenuity.

hidden.label: Hidden
hidden.hint: A dotted line. Found only by searching the points it joins, or from someone who knows the place.

open.label: Entrance
open.hint: A way into the Site, at any point.

hidden.label: Hidden entrance
hidden.hint: An optional second way in, known to few.
hidden.placeholder: Who knows of this way in, and how is it found?

states.over: More than the rules ask for

points.label: Mark the points
points.hint: Mark points with circles as features, triangles as dangers and diamonds as treasure. The point left over is erased, and the rest are numbered.
points.roll: Roll the points still to mark

routes.label: Draw the routes
routes.hint: Join neighbouring points with open, closed and hidden routes.
routes.roll: Roll the routes still to draw

reachable.label: Every point can be reached
reachable.hint: Check every point can be got to, even if some routes are closed or hidden.

entrances.label: Place the entrances
entrances.hint: Where the Site has one, put an entrance on any point, and a hidden one if you like.
entrances.roll: Roll the entrances still to place

rules.heading: Breaking the rules
rules.hint: The book’s counts are a starting point. Rearrange them if it suits the Site’s theme better.

bar.eraseHint: Erase this point, with its routes and entrance.

key.name: Name
key.notesPlaceholder: An ancient tomb, a hostile castle, twisting caverns, misty woods spanning the whole Hex…
key.empty: No points yet. Mark some on the map, or roll them.
key.found: Players have found this. Click to hide it.
key.notFound: Players haven’t found this. Click to reveal it.

players.empty: Nothing has been found here yet.

refereeRolls.loomingAgain: A Looming threat twice in a row: treat it as dire weather.

direWeather.name: Dire Weather
direWeather.hint: When the Realm’s lands suffer dire weather. Dire Weather is then rolled as each Phase begins, unless the Company is in a Holding.

risks.winter: In Winter, as in most Realms

refereeRolls.title: Referee Rolls
refereeRolls.intro: Roll a d6 on one of the Referee’s tables. A low roll goes against the players.

odds.intro: A Luck Roll leaves it to one d6. High goes the players’ way, low goes against them.
odds.tableHelp: tells you how things turn out. Use it when no one has named the odds.
odds.oddsHelp: only answer yes or no. Use them when you’ve already told the players how likely it is, as in “a slim chance”. Fortune favours them on the number shown or higher.
odds.notDomain: The table’s Crisis is a bad turn in the moment, not one of a Domain’s Crises.
odds.question: Which way will you read it?
odds.label: {odds} ({needs}+)
odds.hint: Fortune favours the players on {needs} or higher.

results.problem: Problem: something that could turn bad.

passage.name: Passage of Time
passage.hint: At the end of a session, when it isn’t clear how much time should pass.

results.now: A Season or Age passes now.
results.afterNextSession: A Season or Age passes after the next session.
results.continues: The Season or Age goes on.

unresolved.name: Unresolved Situation
unresolved.hint: For an important situation still unresolved as the Season or Age turns.

results.worst: It goes as badly as it possibly could.

blind.name: Travelling Blind
blind.hint: When travellers with no sense of direction, or lost in darkness or mist, try to enter a new Hex.

results.circleBack: They circle back to where they started.
results.drift: They drift a Hex to the {side}.

weather.name: Dire Weather
weather.hint: As each Phase begins, where the land suffers dire weather, as most Realms do in Winter.

results.dire: Dire weather: nobody can leave the Hex or get proper sleep.
results.looming: A looming threat. Rolled twice in a row, it’s dire weather.

results.woe: Troubled by some woe, past or coming.
results.decline: Things feel as if they’re slipping.
results.fine: Good spirits, and nothing much amiss.

sessionEnd.title: Ending a Session
sessionEnd.hint: As each session ends (p16): settle how much time passes, see what became of anything left hanging, and ask the players what they plan next.
sessionEnd.needStep: Settle how much time passes before ending the session.

notices.promised: A roll last session said the time turns as this one ends (p17).

time.title: How much time passes?
time.hint: The group decides (p17). Roll if they’re uncertain.
time.rollHint: Roll Passage of Time (p17) and let the die settle it.

none.label: None
none.hint: Carry on from where you stopped.
none.card: No time passes: the next session picks up where this one left off.

weeks.label: Weeks
weeks.hint: On to the next seasonal event that matters.
weeks.card: Weeks pass, on to the Season’s next event.

months.label: Months
months.card: Months pass, and the Season turns.

years.label: Years
years.hint: A new Age, starting in Spring.
years.card: Years pass, and a new Age begins in Spring.

situations.title: Anything left unresolved?
situations.hint: An important situation left unresolved before the turn changes on a d6 (p17).
situations.rollHint: Roll Unresolved Situations (p17) for this one.
situations.remove: Take this situation off the list

crises.title: Crisis Rolls still owed
crises.hint: These Domains never made this Season’s Crisis Roll (p20), which is best made before the Season turns.

glory.title: Glory
glory.hint: Glory by other means (p6): a Myth resolved, a tournament won, or a battle history will remember.

plans.title: Plans and ambitions
plans.hint: Ask the players what they mean to do next time (p16). It tells you what to get ready, and is written into the Season’s notes under this session.
plans.placeholder: What they mean to do next

recap.title: This session
recap.hint: Written into the Season’s notes on the Toolkit’s Time page.

attack.title: Attack
attack.noWeapons: Nothing is worn or wielded, so this Attack is unarmed and Impaired.
attack.bonusHint: For good intelligence, clever preparation or a tactical edge. +d8 is typical. List several as d6, d12.
attack.specialistHint: Tick when the situation this weapon is made for comes up, to add its specialist die.
attack.weaknessHint: The Knights have learned what can be turned against them, so every Attack that uses it gets this die. Untick it for a blow that doesn’t.
attack.unavailable: Not offered, being broken or all used: {names}.

greater.hint: A Greater effect can knock a weapon or shield away, take off a helm, or smash a shield or weapon made of wood.
greater.waiting: Waits on their {virtue} Save, which ignores it if passed.
greater.title: Greater effect
greater.which: What does the Greater effect do?
greater.otherDetail: Whatever else it does, written in below. Nobody’s sheet changes.
greater.otherEmpty: Write what the Greater effect does.
greater.nothing: Nobody hit that you can change holds a weapon or shield, wears a helm, or carries anything wooden and whole.
greater.pickUp: Tick it on the sheet again once it’s back in hand.
greater.putOn: Tick it on the sheet again once it’s back on.
greater.npcBack: Once it’s back, give them the point of Armour and its word in the note again.

attack.smiteMarkLine: Smite for a lasting mark rather than more Damage: if this Wounds, it leaves its mark (p187).
attack.smiteHint: A VIG Save follows to avoid Fatigue. A lasting mark, such as an eye put out, adds no dice but is left once the blow Wounds (p187).

grant.blastHint: It strikes everybody targeted, each on a card of their own, as an Ability might let it. Not a Feat, so it holds even when Impaired.
grant.ignoresArmourHint: Its Damage comes with Ignore Armour ticked.
grant.strongGambitsHint: Any die of 4 or more spent on a Gambit buys a Strong one, not only a melee 8+.
grant.spiritHint: Past GD, its Damage comes off SPI rather than VIG. Losing at least half their SPI leaves them broken, out of the fight but not dying.
grant.drainHint: If it Wounds, its maker gets back as much VIG as the target lost, up to their most.
grant.sleepHint: If it Wounds, the target falls into a normal sleep.
grant.memoryHint: If it Wounds, the target is shown one of the attacker’s memories.
grant.shattersHint: Each weapon it’s made with is marked broken once the Attack is rolled, until mended. Shields are left whole.
grant.aloneHint: Nobody may join this Attack, and it can’t be made as part of another’s.
grant.combineHint: Before the roll, a window lets you join your dice into bigger ones, as big as their faces together: a d4 and a d8 make a d12. Nothing joins past a d12.

attack.lastingHint: Kept for the rest of the fight. Untick it to leave it out of this blow alone.
attack.lastingDrop: A die for the rest of the fight. Click to drop it.
attack.keepBonus: Keep the bonus dice for the rest of the fight
attack.keepBonusHint: They join every Attack this one makes until the Combat ends, as an Ability that grows with each blow says. Each shows among their conditions, with × to drop it.
attack.keepBonusNone: Only somebody in a Combat can keep dice for the rest of the fight.
attack.useAbilityHint: Ticked, this blow has it, and one of the Ability’s uses is spent.
attack.useAbilityFreeHint: An Ability with no limit, so it comes ticked. Untick it for a blow it doesn’t help.
attack.useAbilityChosenHint: Used blow by blow, so it waits to be ticked for the blow it’s used in.

onWound.sleep: If this Wounds, the target falls into a normal sleep.
onWound.memory: If this Wounds, the target is shown one of the attacker’s memories.

needs.melee: {name} is used only in a melee Attack, and a ranged weapon is ticked.
needs.charge: {name} is used only on a mounted charge: tick the charge, or Mounted and Moved this turn.

attack.aloneJoin: {name}’s blow is made alone, so it can’t join another’s Attack.
attack.lingers: {name} burns on {when} where its Damage lands, until washed off.

combine.title: Join Dice
combine.hint: Only with at least one ally attacking too. Put dice in the same group to join them into one die as big as their faces together. Leave a die alone to roll it as it is.
combine.over: Group {groups} comes to no die up to a d12.

reroll.hint: Once per Attack, roll every die on this joint Attack again, before anything is spent or declared on them.
reroll.closed: The pool can’t be rolled again now: it already was, nobody has joined, or something has been spent on the dice.
reroll.none: None of the Knights you play in this Attack has an Ability ready to roll the pool again.

sigil.hint: A die shows the number a Knight’s rune is etched for: turn it to another of its faces, spending one of the rune’s turns.
sigil.toHint: Any other face of that die.
sigil.turnHint: {name}’s rune is etched for {number}, with {left} turns left before sunset.
sigil.badValue: That die shows {result}. Turn it to another face, from 1 to {faces}.
sigil.none: No Knight you play has a rune etched for a number these dice show.

attack.saveInHint: VIG as the rules have it, or another where you rule so, such as CLA to dodge a stab at the eye (p187).
attack.blastHint: Roll separately against everybody in the area.
attack.movedHint: Ticked when the Token has moved this turn in combat. Slow weapons can’t be used after moving, and an Exhausted character can’t Attack.
attack.engaged: Began the turn engaged in melee
attack.engagedHint: Purely ranged weapons can’t be used.
attack.mountedHint: A lance counts as Hefty rather than Long on horseback, so it can be wielded with a shield.
attack.spearwallHint: 3 or more allies in a wall formation, all bearing spears or similar. Enemies can’t Attack on the turn they charge it.
attack.charge: Charging on {steed} at enemies on foot (+{dice})
attack.chargeHint: A steed’s trample joins the Attack when it charges foes who are on foot, but never against a spearwall.
attack.chargeBarred: A steed tramples only enemies on foot, and nobody targeted is on foot: {names}.
attack.confinedImpaired: A Long weapon in a confined space is Impaired: it rolls a single d4 and gains no bonus dice or Feats.
attack.swarmImpaired: An individual Attack at a swarm is Impaired unless it’s a Blast: it rolls a single d4 and gains no bonus dice or Feats.
attack.swarmHint: {name} is a swarm: an Attack at them is Impaired unless it’s a Blast.

setAside.slow: {name} is Slow, so it can’t be used after moving.
setAside.ranged: {name} is purely ranged, so it can’t be used after beginning the turn engaged in melee.
setAside.mountedFoe: {name}’s trample doesn’t join, since a steed tramples only enemies on foot.

refusals.exhausted: {name} is Exhausted, so they can’t Attack after moving this turn.
refusals.spearwall: Enemies of a spearwall can’t Attack on the turn they charge it.
refusals.hefty: Two Hefty items can’t be wielded together.
refusals.long: A Long weapon needs both hands, so it can’t be wielded with anything else.
refusals.hands: A weapon or shield fills a hand, so nobody holds more than two.
refusals.twoWays: A weapon is fought one way at a time, and attacks printed with “or” between them are one or the other, so tick only one.
refusals.allSetAside: Every weapon chosen sits out this Attack, so there’s nothing to Attack with.
refusals.smiteRanged: Smite is only used before a melee Attack.

attack.impaired: Impaired: rolls a single d4 and gains no bonus dice or Feats.
attack.againstIndividualsHint: A Warband’s Attack on individuals gets +d12 and causes Blast Damage.
attack.individualsAll: Ticked, since everybody targeted is an individual: {names}.
attack.individualsNot: Unticked, since not everybody targeted is an individual. Not a single person or beast: {names}.
attack.weaponImpaired: {name} is Impaired by a foe’s Gambit: an Attack with it rolls a single d4 and gains no bonus dice or Feats.
attack.weaponImpairedCard: {name} was Impaired by a foe’s Gambit: it rolls a single d4 and gains no bonus dice or Feats.
attack.impairWhichHint: An Attack made with the weapon named rolls a single d4 on their next turn, while their other weapons still fight, as the crocodile’s jaw is Impaired (p186).
attack.joinHint: Everybody attacking the same target rolls at the same time. Add another combatant’s dice to these: the highest die is the Damage, and any of them can pay for Gambits.
attack.noJoiner: Select the Token of whoever joins this Attack.
attack.joinClosed: Too late to join: a Deny or Gambit has already been declared on this Attack.
attack.joinBlastSeveral: {name}’s Attack is a Blast, which rolls separately against each target, so it can’t join an Attack on several targets. Roll it as an Attack of its own.
attack.cantHarm: {names} can’t be harmed by these blows (p11).
attack.barredNote: Struck-through dice can’t harm {names}, so they don’t count toward the Damage (p11).
attack.leaderHint: Someone in the Warband can add their own Attack dice to its roll, taking whatever Damage the Warband takes until their next turn. Select their Token to list them.
attack.ledBy: {name} leads from the front, suffering the same Damage as the Warband until their next turn.
attack.damageNote: The highest die left is the Damage.
attack.gambitPrompt: {count} dice show 4 or higher: click one to spend it on a Gambit.
attack.gambitPromptOne: One die shows 4 or higher: click it to spend it on a Gambit.
attack.strongPrompt: {count} show 8 or higher, so they could make Strong Gambits.
attack.strongPromptOne: One shows 8 or higher, so it could make a Strong Gambit.
attack.denyPrompt: {names} can still Deny: a SPI Save discards one of these dice.
attack.denyPromptAny: Whoever this hits, or an ally close enough to touch, can still Deny one of these dice with a SPI Save.
attack.takeBack: Click a spent die to take its Gambit back.
attack.gambitSaved: {name} Saved with {total} against {virtue} {target}, and ignores it.
attack.gambitFailed: {name} failed with {total} against {virtue} {target}, so it takes effect.
attack.focusSource: Focus pays for this Gambit instead of a die. {name} then makes a CLA Save, or is Fatigued.
attack.focusPassed: {name} passed the CLA Save with {total} against CLA {target}, and avoids Fatigue.
attack.focusFailed: {name} failed the CLA Save with {total} against CLA {target}, and is Fatigued until they rest.
attack.noSaver: Select the Token of whoever Saves against the Gambit.
attack.unspentGambits: {count} dice still show 4 or higher and could be spent on Gambits.
attack.unspentGambitsOne: One die still shows 4 or higher and could be spent on a Gambit.
attack.dismounted: Being dismounted adds a d6 showing {result} to the dice.
attack.noDenier: Select the Token of whoever Denies, or give your User a character.
attack.cantDeny: Nobody you control can Deny this Attack: they are Fatigued, have already Denied it, or don’t know the Feat.
attack.featUsed: {name} has already used {feat} on this Attack.
attack.noTarget: Target the Tokens this Attack hits, then apply the Damage.
attack.targetsGone: The Tokens this Attack targeted are gone.
attack.cantApply: Only a GM or the target’s owner can apply this Damage.
attack.needsGM: A GM needs to be logged in to change somebody else’s Attack card.
attack.changeRefused: The Attack card changed before that could be recorded.

damage.title: Take Damage
damage.amountHint: The highest die left after Gambits, plus any Bolster.
damage.cover: Behind protective cover, against a ranged Attack (+1 Armour)
damage.shieldwallHint: 3 or more allies in a wall formation, all bearing shields rather than bucklers.
damage.bucklerOnly: A buckler doesn’t make a shieldwall.
damage.shieldwallFormed: On the map, {count} of their side stand together, all bearing shields.
damage.shieldwallFew: On the map, fewer than 3 of their side stand together.
damage.shieldwallUnshielded: On the map, not everyone standing together bears a shield: {names}.
damage.situationalHint: Tick each piece whose Armour counts against this Attack. The Armour above follows.
damage.trapped: {name}’s Trap holds their shield, so its Armour doesn’t count
damage.trapOpen: {name}’s Trap left them open: their Armour doesn’t count
damage.exposed: Exposed (take it as if at 0 GD)
damage.doom: Doom: a cheated death catches up with them. Slain instead of Mortally Wounded.
damage.nonLethalDown: Non-lethal: down and out, but not dying.
damage.sparringDown: Sparring: knocked down, but it’ll be shaken off when the duel ends.
damage.spiritHurt: Shaken in spirit, but not Wounded.
damage.drainedAsk: {name} takes back up to {amount} VIG from {victim}, for their player to write in.

onWound.memory: {name} is shown one of the attacker’s memories.

damage.leaderShares: {name} leads {warband} from the front, so suffers the same {damage} Damage. Apply it from their sheet.

immunity.label: Gets past: {immunity}
immunity.hint: Tick only if this blow can harm them.

warband.label: A Blast or large-scale Attack
warband.hint: Individual Attacks don’t harm a Warband.

structure.label: Fire, a siege weapon or a suitably large creature

outcomes.none: The blow is turned aside. No Damage.
outcomes.scar: Left at exactly 0 GD. Roll a Scar on the die that dealt the blow.
outcomes.spared: Non-lethal: already down and out, it takes nothing more.
outcomes.mortal: Mortally Wounded: dying, and dead within the hour unless someone tends them.
outcomes.broken: Broken: out of the fight, but not dying.
outcomes.warded: {name} takes the Mortal Wound in their place.

structureOutcomes.destroyed: Destroyed at 0 GD. A day of repairs brings its GD back.

scarRoll.title: Roll Scar
scarRoll.die: The die that dealt the Scar
scarRoll.apply: Record the Scar and apply its Virtue Loss and immediate GD increase
scarRoll.settle: Settle this Scar: roll its GD increase now its moment has come
scarRoll.settledRaise: {name} settles: max GD rises by {amount} to {value}.
scarRoll.settledNoRaise: {name} settles, but max GD is already above {limit}, so it doesn’t rise.
scarRoll.patchUpHint: Tend the wounds: clear a Mortal Wound, and settle any Gouge or Tear waiting to be stitched or patched up.

revenge.title: Revenge?
revenge.text: {foe} is brought down. If this is {name}’s revenge, the Humiliation settles: a max GD of 12 or under rises by d6.
revenge.foeHint: Who dealt the Humiliation. Bringing them down asks whether that was the revenge.
revenge.notYours: {name} is another player’s Knight. Only their player, or the Referee, says whether revenge is had.

item.retyped: Read the Property of {count} Knights into weapons, armour and steeds, so their Armour counts and their steeds can charge.
item.companionsRenamed: {count} steeds and companions were named afresh: their own sheet says who owns them, and what the book called a steed sits under its name.
item.heftyHint: One hand, and never two Hefty items at once.
item.longHint: Both hands. Impaired in tight spaces.
item.slowHint: No use to someone who has moved this turn. Also Long.
item.heftyMountedHint: Counts as Hefty rather than Long when the wielder is mounted, as a lance does.
item.rangedHint: Useless to someone who started their turn in melee.
item.blastHint: Attacks everybody in the area, rolled separately for each.
item.ignoresArmourHint: Damage isn’t reduced by the target’s Armour.
item.trampleHint: A steed’s trample. Its rider adds it to their Attack when charging foes who are on foot.
item.specialistHint: A specialist weapon gains an extra die in one situation, and is one category rarer than the weapon it’s made from. Tick it in the Attack dialog when that situation comes up.
item.remedyHint: Using it restores this Virtue to everybody there, and uses it up. Nobody, person or pack beast, can carry two.
item.attackDieHint: Shields strike for d4. Leave blank for armour that never attacks.
item.alternatePlaceholder: Such as ranged, or as a pair

item.woodenHint: A Strong Gambit’s Greater effect can break it.
item.lossHint: A Virtue its bearer loses should something befall it, as a banner falling. Its row gets a button that takes the loss.
item.noHandHint: A bite, a shockwave: struck beside whatever is held, so it doesn’t count against two hands. The Attack dialog opens with it unticked.
item.lingersHint: Where its Damage gets past GD, it leaves an affliction that deals its dice as Damage again each round or each day, until washed off.
item.chanceHint: A chance it holds what’s wanted, as 1 in 2. Its row gets a die to roll it.
item.poisonHint: As strong as it is rare: set its Rarity below.
item.conditionHint: When its Armour counts toward the total. For Only when or Except when, write the situation beside it, and tick It holds now while it does.
item.holdsHint: Whether the situation written beside Counts holds right now.
item.bucklerHint: A shield, but not one that makes a shieldwall.
item.rarityHint: Common things are found anywhere, uncommon ones take a specialist, and rare ones are prized. A specialist weapon is a step rarer than the weapon it’s made from.
item.quantityHint: Leave blank for something nobody counts. Restocked, it fills back up to its full stock and is mended.
item.brokenHint: No use until it’s mended: a broken weapon can’t Attack, and broken armour adds nothing.

afflictions.damageHint: Take its toll now: Damage, which can Wound.

warband.hint: Two-dozen or so fighting as one. Only Blast or large-scale Attacks harm them, and their Attacks on individuals get +d12 and Blast.

free.label: All at once

dialog.title: New Realm
dialog.chooseMaking: Roll a Realm the way Creating a Realm describes (p14), start from a blank map and draw it yourself, or bring in a map you have already drawn on paper?
dialog.drawIntro: Makes a blank Realm for you to draw with the Realm tools. Paint its terrain, draw its river, and lay its Barriers and Landmarks, all from the one palette; its Holdings and Myths are set from the Lay of the Land. Nothing is rolled.
dialog.tracedIntro: Lays a picture of your own map under the hexes and rolls nothing. Your map may have hexes drawn on it, or none at all. You line the picture up with the hex lines, then mark what each hex holds with the terrain brush, so Travel and the Wilderness Roll know the land as well as you do. The players see the whole picture, so use a copy without the Myths, Landmarks and Barriers, and place those on the map afterwards.
dialog.intro: Rolls a Realm the way Creating a Realm describes, on a Scene of 12 by 12 hexes: terrain, a river, four Holdings, six Myths, Landmarks and Barriers.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.seedHint: The same seed, set up the same way, rolls the same Realm.
dialog.secretHint: Players see the terrain, the river and the Holdings. Myths, Landmarks and Barriers stay hidden until you reveal them.

picture.title: Import map
picture.intro: A photograph or scan of a Realm drawn on paper, or a painted map with no hexes on it, laid under the hexes in place of the system's own drawings.
picture.paintNext: The picture is only for show. Once it's lined up, go to Wilderness and paint every hex with the terrain drawn on your map.

picture.relaid: The Realm's hexes now sit the way your map's do.
picture.relaidTrimmed: The Realm's hexes now sit the way your map's do. Rivers and Barriers whose hexes no longer meet were cut back.

layouts.legend: Which of these looks like your map?
layouts.hint: Look at the hexes in the top left corner of your map, and pick the drawing that matches them. If your map has no hexes, pick No hexes on it.
layouts.evenColumns: Flat-topped hexes. The corner hex sits higher than the one beside it.
layouts.oddColumns: Flat-topped hexes. The corner hex sits lower than the one beside it.
layouts.evenRows: Pointed-topped hexes. The corner hex sticks out further left than the one under it.
layouts.oddRows: Pointed-topped hexes. The corner hex is set in from the one under it.
layouts.bare: No hexes drawn on it, such as a painted map. The Realm lays its own hexes over the whole picture.

bare.sizeNext: Your map has no hexes on it, so the Realm lays its own over it. You choose how many on the Map size page.
bare.keepsRealmSize: Your map is laid under this Realm's {cols} by {rows} hexes, just large enough to cover them all. A Realm keeps its size once it's made, so for a different number of hexes, make a New Realm from this map.
bare.sizeIntro: Your map has no hexes on it, so the Realm lays its own over it. Choose how many go across, and the rows follow your map's shape, so the hexes cover it edge to edge. Change the rows and the hexes across follow instead. Or use Fewer hexes and More hexes under the map to change both at once. It starts at about as many hexes as a typical Realm's 12 by 12. A side can run to {side} hexes, with up to {hexes} in all, so even a very wide or tall map is covered.
bare.preview: The hexes as they'll lie over your map. Anything shaded falls outside the Realm and isn't shown.
bare.noPicture: Choose your map on the Import map page to see the hexes drawn over it here.
bare.unreadable: Your map couldn't be loaded, so the hexes can't be drawn over it. Check it on the Import map page, or choose it again.
bare.cropped: Your map is a different shape from this Realm's {cols} by {rows} hexes, so a good part of it falls outside the Realm. For hexes that cover all of it, make a New Realm from this map.
bare.slideHint: Your map is laid under the hexes, covering them edge to edge. To move the hexes over it, drag the map; the arrow keys nudge it (Shift for more). Ctrl and the mouse wheel size it about the pointer (Shift for more), which makes the hexes smaller or larger on your map. Then keep it here.

picture.drawnSizeIntro: Your map needn’t be the book’s 12 by 12 hexes. Count the hexes drawn on it, and set how many go across and how many down. Until you set both, the other follows your map’s shape. Fewer hexes and More hexes under the map change both at once, keeping its shape. A side can run to {side} hexes, with up to {hexes} in all.

sizeWindow.open: See the map larger, and set its hexes there
sizeWindow.title: Map size

picture.drawnPreview: The Realm’s hexes over your map, to count yours against. They needn’t sit exactly on yours yet: you line the two up once the Realm is made.

shape.wide: Your map is wider than the book’s Realm Sheet, so it starts at a size that fits its shape rather than 12 by 12 hexes. Check it on the Map size page, where the hexes are drawn over your map. If your map has no hexes drawn on it, choose No hexes on it.
shape.tall: Your map is taller than the book’s Realm Sheet, so it starts at a size that fits its shape rather than 12 by 12 hexes. Check it on the Map size page, where the hexes are drawn over your map. If your map has no hexes drawn on it, choose No hexes on it.

picture.lineUpHint: Once the picture is in, you line it up with the hexes. A map with hexes on it is sized to two of them that you mark, then slid the last little way under the hex lines.
