picture.keepsSize: The imported map can't be sized by hand. Line it up again: it's sized evenly there, by the hexes you mark or with Ctrl and the mouse wheel.

lineUp.first: Click the centre of {hex} on your picture, the first hex of the map, at its top left.
lineUp.second: Now click the centre of {hex}, the last hex of the map, at its bottom right. Drag a mark to move it.
lineUp.adjust: Drag each mark until it sits squarely over its hex on your picture: {first} and {second}. They're drawn as large as your picture's hexes. The arrow keys nudge the one you moved last (Shift for more). Then fit the map to them.
lineUp.tooClose: Those two marks can't be the map's corners. Drag them onto its first hex, at the top left, and its last, at the bottom right.
lineUp.done: The map is lined up. Now paint every hex with the terrain drawn on your map: the picture is only for show, and the Realm knows a hex only by the terrain you paint on it.
lineUp.stopped: The picture is back where it was. Line it up again from the Realm tools whenever you like.
lineUp.missing: There's no picture under this Realm to line up.

steps.slide: Step 2 of 2: Slide it into place.

slide.fitHint: Size the picture evenly and move it so the two marks land on the map's first and last hex (Enter).
slide.keepHint: Keep the picture where it is now, for everyone (Enter).

landmarks.monumentHint: The Phase is spent here, so turn the calendar on when the Company moves.
landmarks.hazardWhich: Pushing through costs d6 of a Virtue, most often VIG. Which does this Hazard take?

goBack.done: The Company goes back the way it came, to {hex}. Travelling there takes the Phase as usual.
goBack.noToken: Only the Company’s own Token can be sent back. Move the Company’s Tokens back by hand.
goBack.unknown: The Company’s way here isn’t known, so move its Token back by hand.

landmarks.hazardIntro: Everybody who pushes through loses d6 {virtue}.
landmarks.ruinEchoes: The ruin echoes this Myth, which the Realm doesn’t hold.
landmarks.promptFrom: Named from the prompts on {myth}’s page (p{page}). Rename it in the Lay of the Land.
landmarks.promptUnread: Import PDF hasn’t read the prompts along the foot of that Myth’s page, so the Landmark keeps its name.
landmarks.ruinHint: Hint at it however the ruin would: a carving, a name half-worn away, a warning nobody living remembers. It may yet return to the Realm.

offCourse.title: Thrown Off Course
offCourse.struck: Travel in the next Phase is travelling blind.
offCourse.pending: A Curse has thrown the Company off course. If they travel in the next Phase, roll Travelling Blind.
offCourse.live: This is the Phase the Curse blights. Travel now counts as travelling blind.
offCourse.rollHint: Roll Travelling Blind for the Company, and let the Curse’s blight go.
offCourse.holdHint: Let the blight go without rolling, because the Company didn’t travel or found their way regardless.

look.title: Realm Appearance
look.hint: Choose how a Realm Scene is drawn: a skin, shipped or made of your own pictures, and a set of colours. Each Realm Scene keeps its own look.
look.intro: Try a skin and a set of colours below, and the Realm Scene you're viewing shows them, for you only. Close this window to put things back. Apply them, and only that Realm Scene is redrawn, with its paper, hex lines and Barriers in the new colours; other Realms keep their own look. New Realms start with the look you last applied. Nothing about the Realm itself changes.

target.none: No Realm Scene in view: changing the look new Realms start with

sheet.label: Blank Realm
sheet.hint: The Blank Realm sheet’s own inked terrain, Holdings and Landmarks, with rivers as the Realm Sheets draw them.

classic.label: Roundels
classic.hint: Pale hexes, fine marks and lettered roundels.

woodcut.label: Woodcut

atlas.label: Surveyor’s Atlas
atlas.hint: Soft washes, fine marks and silhouettes.

armorial.label: Armorial
armorial.hint: Charges from old heraldry books: castles, crowns and beasts drawn in ink, Myths on shields.

own.title: A Skin of Your Own
own.intro: Give the skin a name, then add pictures. Once saved, it’s a skin like the others in Realm Appearance, here and in every other world on this Foundry server.
own.name: Name
own.picturesIntro: Name each file after the picture it replaces, such as forest.png or holding-castle.webp. Any picture you don’t give comes from the skin chosen above.
own.namesHint: The terrain-, holding- and landmark- part can be left off, such as marsh, tower or ruin. Any image type works. Ticked names are given.
own.ignored: {count} files weren’t taken: their names don’t match a Realm picture.
own.needsName: Give the skin a name first.
own.needsPictures: Add at least one picture first.
own.saved: {name} is saved, and can be chosen in every world on this server.
own.removeConfirm: Take {name} off the list of skins, in every world on this server? Realms already drawn with it keep their pictures.
own.loose: This Realm uses pictures of your own that aren’t a saved skin. Choosing a skin replaces them.

look.appliedDefault: New Realms will start with this look.

realmDrawing.title: Creating a Realm
realmDrawing.intro: The players’ copy of the map shows the Holdings and the lie of the land, but not the Myths, Landmarks or Barriers.

paintEveryHex.heading: Paint every hex
paintEveryHex.text: Your map is only a picture: the system can't see what's drawn on it. Pick a terrain below and paint each hex that holds it on your map, until every hex is painted. Travel, the Wilderness Roll and the Lay of the Land go by the terrain you paint, not by the picture. Paint open sea as Lake, the rules' only water, which boats can cross. Nothing stops the Company walking onto a Lake, so rule on that at the table.

realmDrawing.inspectHint: Click a hex, then set it under Edit this hex in the Lay of the Land.

terrain.text: Paint patches of the same terrain, each about d12 hexes.

barriers.text: Outline Barriers along the edges of about one Hex in six. Nothing crosses a Barrier by ordinary means.

river.text: Run a navigable river across the Realm, and add a few big lakes, each filling a Hex or more.

holdings.text: Place 4 Holdings well apart, such as castles, towers, fortresses or walled towns, each ruled by a Knight or a powerful Vassal. Make one the Seat of Power.

myths.text: Put 6 Myths (p27) somewhere remote, numbered 1 to 6.

landmarks.text: Draw 3 or 4 Landmarks of each kind, each marked with an initial or an icon.

dwelling.label: Dwellings
dwelling.text: Where ordinary folk live, out in the wild.

sanctum.label: Sanctums
sanctum.text: Where a Seer lives. Which Seer is found on the Knight table (p26).

monument.label: Monuments
monument.text: An inspiring place. Spending a Phase here restores SPI, as a Sacrament would.

hazard.label: Hazards
hazard.text: The land itself resists. Find a way, push on at a cost of d6 VIG, or turn back.

curse.label: Curses
curse.text: A blight that leads travellers astray: travel in the next Phase is travelling blind (p18).

ruin.label: Ruins
ruin.text: A relic that foretells: it hints at a Myth not active in the Realm, which may yet return.

tally.seatMany: {count} Seats of Power, where the sheet has one
tally.seatDisputed: {count} Holdings claim the Seat of Power

company.intro: Choose what the Company looks like, then carry them over the map and click the hex they stand in.
company.standing: The Company stands in {hex}. Choose another picture, or take them up and stand them somewhere else.

finish.hint: Done drawing: bring back Travel and Exploration and whisper the GMs the Realm's key.
finish.title: Finish the Realm
finish.short: This Realm has less than a typical one:
finish.anyway: These numbers are a guide, not a law (p14). Finish the Realm as it is?
finish.done: {name} is drawn. Travel and Exploration are back beside the map.

realmDrawing.credit: Creating a Realm (p14), summed up in the system’s own words. Run Import PDF to read the rulebook’s own page here.
realmDrawing.bookCredit: Creating a Realm, read from your copy of the rulebook by Chris McDowall, Bastionland Press (p14).

warband.full: Every Warband this Holding can raise is in the field.
warband.cantCreate: Mustering a Warband creates an actor, so it needs a user who is allowed to create actors. Ask the Referee.

vassals.label: Loyal Vassals
vassals.hint: Those who serve the Holding, called up from their fields and workshops.
vassals.text: Drawn from loyal Vassals, who leave their own work to serve.

allies.label: Knights Who Share a Cause
allies.hint: Knights who ride with you because your cause is theirs.
allies.text: Drawn from Knights who share the cause, and who expect it to be honoured.

mercenaries.label: Mercenaries
mercenaries.hint: Soldiers who fight for an agreed price.
mercenaries.text: Hired swords with a price agreed, who will see it paid.

muster.title: Muster a Warband
muster.hint: A Seat of Power can usually raise 3 Warbands, any other Holding 2.
muster.origin: Where the soldiers are drawn from
muster.blankIntro: Who takes the field for {name}? Import PDF brings in the book’s Warbands; until then, raise one and fill in their stats.
muster.blankDetail: No stats yet. Fill them in on their sheet.
muster.needs: Wherever they come from, soldiers expect to be fed and sheltered while they serve.
muster.marshal: Their training and arms are the Marshal’s business.
muster.full: {name} already has {count} Warbands in the field, all it can raise. Muster another anyway?

dismiss.title: Disband
dismiss.confirm: Disband {name}? Its soldiers leave the service of {domain}. Their sheet stays in the Actors tab.
dismiss.went: {name} is disbanded and leaves the service of {domain}.

upkeep.title: Upkeep
upkeep.hint: A Warband short of rest or food, or driven too hard, loses d6 SPI.
upkeep.needs: Soldiers expect to be fed and sheltered while they serve.
upkeep.notDamage: Virtue Loss is not Damage, so it can never Mortally Wound or Slay them.
upkeep.broken: At SPI 0 {name} stops taking orders and looks out only for itself.

illRested.label: Ill-rested
illRested.text: Night after night without proper sleep.

poorlyFed.label: Poorly fed
poorlyFed.text: Short rations, and no sight of better.

pushedTooFar.label: Driven too hard
pushedTooFar.text: Asked for more than soldiers have to give.

fallen.title: A Knight Falls
fallen.text: Death comes for bold Knights too, often suddenly and without honour. Their player makes another Knight, who joins the Company soon, or takes up a successor, Squire or follower.
fallen.successorNotYours: Only the Referee can hand {name} to you. Ask them to press this.
fallen.whichFollower: Who rode with {name}, and who takes up the journey now?
fallen.tookUp: {name} takes up the Company’s journey where {fallen} left it.
fallen.notYours: {name} was another player’s Knight. Only their player, or the Referee, says who carries on.
fallen.cantCreate: Making a new Knight creates an actor, so it needs a user who is allowed to create actors. Ask the Referee.

explore.mark: Mark it on the players’ map
explore.markedNothing: The players’ map already shows all of it.

folklore.title: Gathering Folklore
folklore.intro: Somebody in {hex} is asked what they know of the Realm.
folklore.freely: Knowledge like that comes at a price. What they want in return is for the table to settle.

vassal.label: A Vassal
vassal.hint: Knows the nearest Myth and which way it lies (exactly where, if it’s next to their home), and the Landmarks in and around their home Hex.

roamer.label: A Knight or Vagabond
roamer.hint: Has travelled enough to know one Myth of the Realm, picked at random, and roughly where it lies, and the nearest Landmark.

seer.label: A Seer
seer.hint: Knows every Myth’s rules, secrets, weaknesses and cures, where each lies, and every Landmark in the Realm.

folklore.nothing: They know of no Myth and no Landmark from here.
folklore.rumours: They’ve heard warnings of danger, but nothing of how to escape or undo it.
folklore.secrets: They know this Myth’s rules and secrets, what it’s weak to, and how to cure the harm it does.

search.title: Searching
search.intro: A whole Phase is spent searching {hex}.
search.aim: What the Phase is spent on

sweep.label: Sweep the whole Hex
sweep.hint: A quick look over the whole Hex.

known.label: Search for something known to be here
known.hint: Hunting properly for something known to be there: an action like any other, with a Save.

vantage.label: Climb somewhere high
vantage.hint: Climb to somewhere the Hex and the land around it can be taken in.

search.ifItCalls: If there’s a Save to make
search.virtueHint: The Company picks who rolls, with their own Virtue. Choose the Virtue for whatever the risky part mostly is.
search.rolledHint: If they rolled the d20 at the table, enter what it showed. Leave it empty to roll here.
search.phaseHint: A search uses up a whole Phase. Untick it where the Referee rules otherwise.
search.obstacle: They may still manage it, but something now stands in the way: an obstacle, a hostile meeting, or a price. The land has moods of its own: bad weather, shifting ground.
search.noOne: Nobody was chosen to roll the Save, so nothing was rolled.

survey.seat: The Seat of Power stands here: {name}.
survey.myth: Myth {number} has plainly left its mark on this Hex.
survey.sweepHint: A sweep takes in the Hex itself. What lies in the Hexes around it waits on the Wilderness Roll.
survey.vantageHint: From up high they take in this Hex and get a rough idea of the land around, but nothing precise: the Myths and Landmarks hidden out there keep their secrets.

settingsTab.intro: Your own settings, kept in this browser. They change how Mythic Bastionland’s sheets, windows and chat cards look for you, and nobody else at the table sees the difference.

attackFx.name: Attack Effects on the Map
attackFx.hint: When on, an Attack is drawn on the map and heard at the table: every weapon that added a die strikes in turn, the biggest die first, so a sword swings and the shield on the arm follows it. An arrow flies, a beast’s jaws close, and a mounted charge comes at a gallop. Applying the Damage bursts on whoever lost GD, bloodies whoever lost VIG, and clanks where the Armour took the whole blow. The pictures need the Sequencer and JB2A modules, and the sounds the SoundFx Library module; without them, that half does nothing. Anyone who has turned on Reduce Motion, here or in their browser, keeps the sounds without the pictures.

phaseBannerShown.name: Phase, Season and Age at the Top of the Screen
phaseBannerShown.hint: Show the Phase of the Day, the Season and the Age at the top of the screen, the Phase and the Season in the same colours as the cards their changes post to chat. Untick to hide them in this browser only: everyone else keeps theirs.

visitedMarksShown.name: Mark the Hexes the Company Has Been To
visitedMarksShown.hint: Mark every hex of a Realm the Company has come into. Untick to hide them in this browser only: everyone else keeps theirs. The footprints beside the sidebar do the same, and a right-click on them chooses the mark.

hexReadoutShown.name: Name the Realm Hex under the Pointer
hexReadoutShown.hint: Pointing at a hex of a Realm shows a label under the map naming its terrain and what stands there. Untick to hide it in this browser only: everyone else keeps theirs.

travelRulesShown.name: Travel Rules beside the Realm Map
travelRulesShown.hint: Show Travel on the left of a Realm’s map and Rest and Exploration on its right. Untick to hide them in this browser only: everyone else keeps theirs. A GM who hides them hides the rolls and the Lose d6 buttons they hold too.

restoreOpenSheets.name: Reopen Sheets on Reload
restoreOpenSheets.hint: Reopen the Knight, item and journal sheets and the rulebook you had open, where you left them, when you reload Foundry. Only affects this browser.

textSize.name: Text Size
textSize.hint: Make the writing on Mythic Bastionland’s sheets, windows and chat cards larger or smaller, and the pictures beside it with it. 1.00 is the size they were drawn at.

contrast.name: Contrast
contrast.hint: High Contrast puts Mythic Bastionland’s sheets, windows and chat cards on plain white paper in black ink, and darkens the faint and coloured writing on them. Pair it with a larger Text Size.

typeface.name: Typeface
typeface.hint: The lettering on Mythic Bastionland’s sheets, windows and chat cards. Old Print is the printed book’s look. The other two are plainer to read, and set the blackletter titles in small capitals.
typeface.book: Old Print, as in the Book
typeface.signika: Signika, as in Foundry’s Own Windows

noItalics.name: No Italic Text
noItalics.hint: Set every slanted word upright, everywhere in Foundry and not only on Mythic Bastionland’s sheets. Italics are harder to read, the old print’s most of all, and more so under a magnifier. The trade is that italics mark some things out, such as the hint under a field, and those will read like the text around them.

reduceMotion.name: Reduce Motion
reduceMotion.hint: Turn off the fades on Mythic Bastionland’s sheets and windows, and move the map straight to a hex shown from the GM Toolkit instead of panning there.

keywordTips.name: Rule Word Popups
keywordTips.hint: Hovering a rule word, such as Exposed, Hefty or Gambit, in Mythic Bastionland’s windows and chat cards shows what the book says it means.

artPreviews.name: Larger Art on Hover
artPreviews.hint: Show a larger copy of a Knight’s, Seer’s or Myth’s picture beside it while the pointer is over it.

dice.again: {dice} gave {total} — click to roll it again

keywords.unread: Explained on p{page} of the rulebook.

portrait.stage: The whole picture, with the part the sheet shows boxed
portrait.frameHint: Drag inside the box to move it, a corner to resize it, or anywhere outside to draw a new one. Arrow keys nudge it, with Shift for bigger steps, and + or − resize it.
portrait.loadFailed: This picture couldn't be loaded to frame.
portrait.video: A moving picture can't be framed.

artPopout.shown: Showed the picture of {name} to the players.
artPopout.nobodyToShow: No one else is signed in to show the picture to.

rulebook.title: Mythic Bastionland
rulebook.nobodyToShow: No one else is signed in to show the page to.
rulebook.noCopy: The GM hasn’t given this world a copy of the rulebook yet.
rulebook.otherEdition: This PDF has {pages} pages, but the rulebook this system’s page numbers come from has {expected}, so a jump to a page may land in the wrong place.
rulebook.notPdf: That file doesn’t look like a PDF. It’s been saved anyway, in case it is one.
rulebook.copying: Copying the rulebook into the world…
rulebook.copied: The rulebook is ready to read.

keybinding.name: Open the Rulebook
keybinding.hint: Open the rulebook, or close it when it’s already in front.

forPlayers.name: Let Players Open the Rulebook
forPlayers.hint: Players get the Rulebook button and hotkey too. Pages the GM shows them open either way.

setup.title: Your Rulebook
setup.intro: Point this world at your own copy of the Mythic Bastionland PDF to read it in Foundry’s PDF viewer, with its chapters, search and page links.
setup.choose: Choose a File on This Computer
setup.copyHint: A file chosen from this computer is copied to {dir} in your Foundry data folder, so it’s still there next session. Forgetting it leaves the file there.
setup.importHint: Whichever way you point this world at the book, its art and tables are imported from it as well.
setup.whoCanRead: Foundry serves everything in its data folder to anyone signed into the world who knows the path, so treat the copy as shared with your table.
setup.hotkey: Press B to open or close the rulebook. Change the key under Configure Controls.

realmTour.title: Your First Realm
realmTour.description: Where Realms are made: the Scenes tab, and the New Realm button at its top.

scenes.title: The Scenes Tab
scenes.content: Each Realm is a Scene of its own, kept here with the world’s other Scenes.

newRealm.title: New Realm
newRealm.content: New Realm makes a Realm for the Company to travel. Roll it from the book’s tables, draw it yourself on a blank map, or import a map you drew on paper.

realmButtonsTour.title: The Realm’s Buttons
realmButtonsTour.description: The two buttons beside the sidebar on a Realm: Mark the Hexes Visited, and Places.

marks.title: Mark the Hexes Visited
marks.content:
The footprints mark every hex the Company has been to on the map, or hide the marks again. Each player chooses for their own browser.
Right-click them to choose the mark: a pencilled ring, a tick, a cross or the hex’s edge, each in a colour of your choosing.

places.title: Places
places.content:
Places opens the record of where the Company has been: each hex it has visited, what was found there and the notes kept on it.
Players have the same button, and see only the places their Company has found.

welcome.title: Welcome to Mythic Bastionland
welcome.hint: The window a new world opens with, where your rulebook PDF is brought in.
welcome.lead: A game of Knights, Seers and Myths, by Chris McDowall.

book.heading: Your Rulebook
book.intro: The rulebook doesn’t come with this system. If you own the PDF, the {pages}-page one, choose it here and this world is filled in from it.

found.pending: We already have your rulebook: the PDF you brought into another world is on this server, so there’s nothing to choose. What this world needs from it is imported by itself.
found.importing: We already have your rulebook: the PDF you brought into another world is on this server, so there’s nothing to choose. Importing what this world needs from it now…
found.done: We already had your rulebook: the PDF you brought into another world is on this server, and what this world needs from it has been imported. There was nothing to choose.

art.label: The art and tables
art.hint: Every Knight’s, Seer’s and Myth’s picture, the text the choosers fill characters in from, the Spark Tables, and compendiums of Arms & Goods. The PDF is read in your browser, and what’s taken from it is saved to {root} in your Foundry data folder.

keep.label: A copy to read in Foundry
keep.hint: Always kept. Opens with B, or the Rulebook button in the Journal tab, with its chapters and search. It’s copied to {dir} in your Foundry data folder, which anyone signed into the world can fetch if they know the path.
keep.done: This world reads its rulebook from

book.later: Later on, Import PDF on the hotbar and the Rulebook button in the Journal tab both do this again.

company.heading: The Company
company.question: How many Knights have followed the call to glory?
company.waiting: Signed in and waiting for a Knight: {names}. Each is given one, and it opens on their screen for them to choose.
company.nobody: No players are signed in yet. The count follows them as they join; Knights nobody is signed in for wait in the Actors tab, where Played by on the sheet gives them to a player.
company.left: Still in the Actors tab for a player: {count}.
company.failed: The Company’s Knights couldn’t all be made. The console says why.

knights.text: Create Actor in the Actors tab makes a Knight, then offers to roll or pick one from the book.

realms.text: New Realm in the Scenes tab draws a Realm map to explore, hex by hex.

sites.text: New Site in the Journal tab, or on the hotbar, maps a Site that players see as they explore it.

referee.text: Referee Rolls, Spark Tables, Time and the GM Toolkit, where the Myths and their Omens are kept, wait in the Roll Tables tab.

import.title: Your Rulebook
import.text: Choose your Mythic Bastionland PDF to keep a copy to read in Foundry and to import its art and tables.

realm.title: Your First Realm
realm.text: Roll a Realm from the book’s tables, or draw one yourself, for the Company to explore.

modules.title: Recommended Modules
modules.text: Nothing here needs them, but each makes the table better. Install them from the Add-on Modules tab on Foundry’s setup screen, then turn them on for this world.

diceSoNice.name: Dice So Nice!
diceSoNice.text: rolls every Save, Attack and table roll as three-dimensional dice on the table.

sequencer.name: Sequencer and JB2A
sequencer.text: draw each Attack on the map: swords swing, arrows fly, and Damage bursts or bloodies whoever it lands on.

soundFx.name: SoundFx Library
soundFx.text: gives those Attacks their sound, heard by everyone at the table.

fxmaster.name: FXMaster
fxmaster.text: draws the weather, set from the GM Toolkit or rolled each morning, on the Scene the players are on.

tokenizer.name: Tokenizer
tokenizer.text: makes round map tokens from Knight and NPC portraits.

scars.disfigurement: A max GD of 2 or under goes up by d6.
scars.stun: Lose d6 CLA. A max GD of 4 or under goes up by d6.
scars.gouge: Once it’s stitched, a max GD of 6 or under goes up by d6.
scars.tear: Once it’s patched, a max GD of 8 or under goes up by d6.
scars.mutilation: By next Season there’s a prosthetic, or a way of managing without, and a max GD of 10 or under goes up by d6.
scars.doom: A Mortal Wound this Season Slays instead.
scars.humiliation: Once revenge is had, a max GD of 12 or under goes up by d6.
